# hoba — Hiring Obstacles & Barriers Atlas

> A public, versioned, machine-readable registry of what goes wrong in hiring and what can be inferred from it. Registry 1.5.0, schema 1.6.0. Content CC BY-SA 4.0, code MIT.

hoba separates an observation from its cause. A rejection email is a signal; the mechanisms that could have produced it are a separate layer; which of them a candidate can act on is a third. The registry never asserts which mechanism fired — only which are compatible, and which probes distinguish them.

## Ontology

- **Observations** (`observation`, 21; IDs obs.* (legacy A-### aliases resolve)) — A directly observable trace left by the hiring process.
- **Barriers** (`barrier`, 16; IDs bar.* (legacy B-### aliases resolve)) — A gate where the nominal hiring path can stop or diverge.
- **Mechanisms** (`mechanism`, 28; IDs mech.* (legacy M-### aliases resolve)) — A causal force compatible with one or more observations and barriers.
- **Patterns** (`pattern`, 4; IDs pat.* (legacy P-### aliases resolve)) — A recurring, rule-defined combination of observations and compatible mechanisms.
- **Loops** (`loop`, 3; IDs loop.* (legacy L-### aliases resolve)) — A validated reinforcing cycle among mechanisms.
- **Interventions** (`intervention`, 24; IDs int.* (legacy I-### aliases resolve)) — An actor-owned change aimed at a barrier, mechanism, pattern, or loop.
- **Actors** (`actor`, 7; IDs actor.*) — A decision seat with explicit controls, blind spots, and incentives.
- **Processes** (`process`, 4; IDs proc.* (legacy WF-### aliases resolve)) — A state machine naming the subject, states, owners, transitions, and expected timing.
- **Eras** (`era`, 4; IDs era.* (legacy E-### aliases resolve)) — A sourced period of hiring economics: capital, hiring behavior, entry paths, and its ending.
- **Evidence records** (`evidence`, 52; IDs evidence.* (legacy EVD-### aliases resolve)) — A language-neutral source supporting registry claims.
- **Financial records** (`record`, 13; IDs record.* (legacy R-### aliases resolve)) — A durable budget, contract, funding, fee, payroll, subscription, or runway state with explicit flows.

Scenarios (11) are validated compositions over canonical IDs. Archetypes (124) are presentation-only overlays. The formal substrate is derived and never authored as a second source of truth.

The graph export is deliberately narrower than the ontology: 96 reader-facing finding nodes and 276 edges over the relations `operates_at`, `emits`, `amplifies`, `masks`, `precedes`, `instantiates`, `targets`, `mitigates`.

## Reading it by machine

- Full registry: https://hoba.work/data/latest/registry.json
- Inventory, boundaries and usage choices: https://hoba.work/data/latest/inventory.json
- One entity: https://hoba.work/api/v1/mechanisms/mech.genuine_technical_skill_shortfall.json
- Any page as Markdown: https://hoba.work/mechanisms/mech.genuine_technical_skill_shortfall.md — or the canonical URL with `Accept: text/markdown`
- The whole catalogue as one document: https://hoba.work/registry.md
- Graph: https://hoba.work/data/latest/graph.json · https://hoba.work/data/latest/graph.graphml
- Tabular: https://hoba.work/data/latest/nodes.csv · https://hoba.work/data/latest/edges.csv
- Schema: https://hoba.work/data/latest/schema.json · OpenAPI: https://hoba.work/openapi.json
- This file in full: https://hoba.work/llms-full.txt

An MCP server ships in the repository (`packages/mcp`) exposing search, entity lookup, the diagnostic protocol, pattern matching and graph traversal over stdio.

## What it will not do

- It does not name or rank employers, and it holds no company records.
- It does not attribute intent. Mechanisms describe structure, not motive.
- Document excerpts on the site are reconstructions, written to be typical, and are labelled as such. They are not captured records.

---

## Observations

### obs.communication_mismatch_or_tone_friction_in_panel — Communication mismatch or tone friction in panel

Noticeable divergence in communication style, pacing, or terminology during live panel discussions.

- Stages: recruiter, team · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not prove the candidate lacks teamwork skills in general.
- Probe [PROBE-A-010-1] (low): Ask the recruiter for explicit feedback on the collaborative dynamic. → Clarifies whether the friction was taken as an attitude issue or as a difference in style.

### obs.compensation_band_reduced_or_altered_mid_process — Compensation band reduced or altered mid-process

The compensation band offered or discussed is revised downward from the range previously agreed or advertised.

- Stages: recruiter, compensation, offer · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not prove an intentional bait-and-switch unless evidence of company policy establishes one.
- Probe [PROBE-A-005-1] (medium): Ask whether the revised band follows from a lower levelling grade or from a company-wide budget adjustment. → Separates the outcome of the levelling assessment from the company's financial constraints.

### obs.complete_silence_after_submission — Complete silence after submission

After the application is submitted, nothing arrives: no automated receipt, no acknowledgement, no rejection, no message from a recruiter.

- Stages: ingestion, sourcing · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not prove the application was reviewed by a human.
- Does NOT establish: Does not prove the role was cancelled or already filled.
- Probe [PROBE-A-001-1] (low): Check the email spam folder and the security quarantine for an automated acknowledgement from the ATS. → Shows whether the application was ingested and generated a confirmation ID.

### obs.conflicting_feedback_across_different_interviewers — Conflicting feedback across different interviewers

Feedback from one round praises architectural depth while another round claims insufficient technical background.

- Stages: technical, team · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not prove bad faith; it shows the rubric was not calibrated across the hiring committee.
- Probe [PROBE-A-014-1] (low): Ask the talent partner for the consolidated rubric summary. → Shows whether the two rounds were scoring against different criteria.

### obs.explicit_feedback_citing_skill_depth_shortfall — Explicit feedback citing skill-depth shortfall

Interviewer or recruiter provides structured notes citing a specific deficit in algorithmic complexity, architecture, or tool mastery.

- Stages: technical, team · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not imply general incompetence; it reflects the threshold for this specific role level.
- Probe [PROBE-A-008-1] (medium): Review the interview solution against the standard patterns for that problem and identify the edge cases it misses. → Verifies whether the code actually lacked the optimisation or rigour the notes name.

### obs.feedback_naming_as_absent_something_the_submitted_work_contains — Feedback naming as absent something the submitted work contains

The stated shortfall is the absence of work that is present in what the candidate submitted, at the path they gave.

- Stages: screening, technical · Evidence: compatible
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the work was never opened, only that the claim and the submission disagree.
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the work would have met the bar had it been read.
- Probe [PROBE-A-019-1] (low): Open the submitted path in a private window with no session, and note what the first screen shows before any navigation. → Establishes what a reader with no context and no time actually lands on.

### obs.feedback_stating_candidate_is_overqualified_for_the_grade — Feedback stating candidate is overqualified for the grade

Candidate is rejected on the grounds that their experience, seniority, or previous scope sits above the band the role was opened at.

- Stages: recruiter, screening, team · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not imply the candidate is undesirable; what it names is a concern about retention and about a pay mismatch.
- Probe [PROBE-A-013-1] (low): Ask whether the organisation has requisitions open at a higher band or at staff level, where the wider scope is part of the role. → Shows whether anything is open above this band.

### obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template — Generic "closer alignment" rejection template

A standard automated email saying that the team has decided to proceed with candidates whose profiles match the requirements of the role more closely.

- Stages: ingestion, screening, recruiter, technical, hiring-manager, team, compensation, offer, post-offer · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish which specific skill was deemed insufficient.
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish whether a human reviewer read the full resume.
- Probe [PROBE-A-002-1] (low): Compare the wording of the CV with the exact requirement phrases in the published job description. → Reveals a possible vocabulary mismatch between the candidate's wording and the ATS rubric.

### obs.materially_similar_role_reposted_shortly_after_rejection — Materially similar role reposted shortly after rejection

The same listing, or a near-identical one, is reposted or refreshed on the job boards within 1–8 weeks of the rejection.

- Stages: sourcing, screening, technical · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the role was a "fake" or "ghost" posting.
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the prior interview feedback was fraudulent.
- Probe [PROBE-A-004-1] (low): Check the requisition ID on the listing, or ask the recruiter whether the posting is an automated ATS refresh or a separate headcount opening. → Distinguishes an automated refresh on the job board from a genuinely recurring hiring need.

### obs.multiple_interview_reschedulings_or_interviewer_no_show — Multiple interview reschedulings or interviewer no-show

Interviews are postponed repeatedly or moved at short notice, or the interviewer does not join the call at the scheduled time.

- Stages: recruiter, technical, team · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not imply candidate rejection; frequently reflects interviewer calendar congestion or emergency incidents.
- Probe [PROBE-A-007-1] (low): Offer a set of concrete times you are free, and confirm the contact details 2 hours before the call. → Minimises scheduling friction and shows how quickly the recruiter answers.

### obs.offer_accepted_followed_by_delayed_start_date_or_post_signing_revocation — Offer accepted followed by delayed start date or post-signing revocation

A signed offer is met with repeated start-date delays, pre-day-one communication freezes, or sudden revocation during early onboarding.

- Stages: post-offer · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the candidate's performance or background check caused the delay.
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the role was fraudulent when the offer was originally issued.
- Probe [PROBE-A-020-1] (low): Request written confirmation of the revised start date alongside written clarification of whether hardware shipment and payroll registration remain active. → Separates an administrative IT delay from a structural hiring freeze or pre-start headcount cancellation.

### obs.offer_rescinded_or_delayed_due_to_internal_freeze — Offer rescinded or delayed due to internal freeze

Candidate is offered a role verbally or in writing, and the offer is then delayed or withdrawn before the start date.

- Stages: offer, post-offer · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not mean the candidate failed a reference check, unless the message says so.
- Probe [PROBE-A-011-1] (low): Ask for written notice of whether the requisition is cancelled outright or deferred to the next fiscal quarter. → Establishes whether there is a date to wait for.

### obs.position_closed_after_final_interview_without_hire — Position closed after final interview without hire

The candidate completes every interview round and then learns that the requisition has been cancelled, frozen, or closed.

- Stages: team, offer · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not prove that the candidate failed the technical or behavioural evaluations.
- Does NOT establish: Does not prove that the company misstated its intention in opening the role.
- Probe [PROBE-A-003-1] (low): Ask the recruiter whether the role was closed by a budget restructuring or by a reallocation of the work inside the team. → Clarifies whether the barrier was specific to this candidate or budgetary.

### obs.rejection_after_the_application_sat_pending_for_months — Rejection after the application sat pending for months

A rejection arrives six weeks or more after submission, with no contact in the interval and no stage ever entered.

- Stages: ingestion, screening · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not mean the application was read at any point during the interval.
- Does NOT establish: Does not mean a decision on the merits was taken at the end of it.
- Probe [PROBE-A-015-1] (low): Compare the date the posting came down with the date the rejection arrived, using the portal's own listing history or a saved copy of the posting. → Establishes whether the message followed the close of the search or an interval counted from submission.

### obs.rejection_naming_a_jurisdiction_or_work_eligibility_ground — Rejection naming a jurisdiction or work-eligibility ground

The stated reason is where the candidate lives, the hours they can cover, or the right to be employed there — not anything about the work.

- Stages: ingestion, recruiter · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that no route to employment existed, only that none was used here.
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the constraint was the first ground on which the application was set aside.
- Probe [PROBE-A-017-1] (low): Compare the ground named in the message against the copy of the posting as it stood on the day of application. → Establishes whether the ground was stated up front or introduced afterwards.

### obs.rejection_naming_a_specific_industry_sector_as_required — Rejection naming a specific industry sector as required

The stated reason is the absence of experience in one named sector, rather than the depth or correctness of the work assessed.

- Stages: recruiter, technical · Evidence: compatible
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the sector was irrelevant to the work.
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the assessed work fell short in any respect.
- Probe [PROBE-A-018-1] (low): Compare the sector named in the message against the requirements section of the posting as it stood on the day of application. → Establishes whether the sector was listed as required, listed as preferred, or absent.

### obs.rejection_naming_an_internal_hire_as_the_outcome — Rejection naming an internal hire as the outcome

The closing message states the role went to someone already inside the organisation, after the candidate had completed the later rounds.

- Stages: team, offer · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the internal candidate was identified before the search was published.
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the external rounds were run without a decision available to them.
- Probe [PROBE-A-016-1] (low): Check whether the posting was withdrawn or remained live, and whether it was reposted with the same level and scope within the following weeks. → Distinguishes a filled requisition from a search that continued after the message.

### obs.rejection_within_minutes_of_application_submission — Rejection within minutes of application submission

Automated rejection email arrives within 2 to 30 minutes of form submission, outside business hours.

- Stages: ingestion · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not mean a human engineer read the resume and judged it poor.
- Probe [PROBE-A-009-1] (low): Audit the application answers to the mandatory knock-out questions (work permit, country of residence, minimum years of experience). → Identifies which boolean filter rule the ATS applied.

### obs.republished_job_posting_with_refreshed_date_and_identical_requirement_body — Republished job posting with refreshed date and identical requirement body

An opening is closed or reposted with an updated timestamp and identical requirement text, resetting applicant queues while preserving candidate pipeline collection.

- Stages: pre-posting, sourcing · Evidence: proven
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that previous applicants were rejected on qualification grounds.
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that a confirmed budget line exists for immediate onboarding.
- Probe [PROBE-A-021-1] (low): Compare the requirement text hash against prior archive snapshots and ask the recruiter if active interviewing has commenced. → Separates an active newly funded replacement hire from an evergreen talent pool or stale posting refresh.

### obs.take_home_assignment_exceeding_reasonable_stated_scope — Take-home assignment exceeding reasonable stated scope

The take-home assignment asks for production-grade features that take 20+ hours to build, against a stated budget of 2–4 hours.

- Stages: technical · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not prove the company is harvesting free intellectual property for production use.
- Probe [PROBE-A-006-1] (low): Write the boundaries and trade-offs into the submission's README, naming the assumptions made to fit the agreed timebox. → Tests whether evaluators value scope management and communication over unbounded free work.

### obs.unsolicited_recruiter_outreach_followed_by_ghosting — Unsolicited recruiter outreach followed by ghosting

Recruiter opens direct outreach expressing strong interest, then stops replying once the candidate answers with availability.

- Stages: sourcing, recruiter · Evidence: supported
- Does NOT establish: Does not prove the profile was rejected; often it is what an automated batch sourcing campaign looks like.
- Probe [PROBE-A-012-1] (low): Send one polite follow-up after five business days, on the original outreach thread. → Recovers a stalled conversation if the recruiter was away or over capacity.

## Barriers

### bar.requisition_approval_public_posting — Requisition Approval & Public Posting

The gate that exists before any candidate does: headcount is authorised, the job description is written, and the requisition is published (or kept open) on careers pages and job boards.

- Stage: pre-posting · Order: 1 · Passes when: An approved requisition with a written job description is published against real, funded headcount.
- Precedes: bar.outbound_sourcing_talent_pool_contact, bar.application_ingestion

### bar.outbound_sourcing_talent_pool_contact — Outbound Sourcing & Talent Pool Contact

Recruiter-initiated outreach to passive candidates and talent-pool building, independent of any inbound application.

- Stage: sourcing · Order: 2 · Passes when: The candidate responds to outreach and is attached to an active, authorised requisition rather than a speculative pool.
- Precedes: bar.application_ingestion, bar.recruiter_screening_call

### bar.application_ingestion — Application Ingestion

The initial ingestion gate where candidate CV and structured application fields enter the talent acquisition database / ATS.

- Stage: ingestion · Order: 3 · Passes when: The application record is received, validates against the minimum schema, and is linked to an active job requisition.
- Precedes: bar.automated_filter_parser_threshold

### bar.automated_filter_parser_threshold — Automated Filter & Parser Threshold

Algorithmic text extraction, keyword scoring, compliance screening (location/work authorisation), and knockout question evaluations.

- Stage: ingestion · Order: 4 · Passes when: The extraction score from CV parsing is at or above the threshold, and the candidate passes every mandatory algorithmic gating rule.
- Precedes: bar.inbound_screening_triage, bar.recruiter_screening_call

### bar.inbound_screening_triage — Inbound Screening & Triage

Recruiter or sourcing coordinator manual review of parsed inbound applications vs active outbound talent pipelines.

- Stage: screening · Order: 5 · Passes when: The recruiter adds the application to the active short-list for a first conversation.
- Precedes: bar.recruiter_screening_call

### bar.recruiter_screening_call — Recruiter Screening Call

Initial conversational interview evaluating salary expectations, timeline, communication, English fluency, and high-level role alignment.

- Stage: recruiter · Order: 6 · Passes when: The recruiter and the candidate agree on the core parameters, and the recruiter submits the candidate to the hiring team.
- Precedes: bar.technical_screen_live_assessment

### bar.technical_screen_live_assessment — Technical Screen / Live Assessment

Synchronous technical evaluation assessing core technical competencies, problem-solving speed, and system architecture fundamentals.

- Stage: technical · Order: 7 · Passes when: The candidate's total on the assessing engineer's rubric is at or above the threshold to advance.
- Precedes: bar.take_home_work_sample_evaluation, bar.hiring_manager_in_depth_review

### bar.take_home_work_sample_evaluation — Take-Home / Work Sample Evaluation

Asynchronous technical assignment or project artifact reviewed by engineering peers against quality benchmarks.

- Stage: technical · Order: 8 · Passes when: The submitted code meets the architecture, functionality, test coverage and documentation requirements.
- Precedes: bar.hiring_manager_in_depth_review

### bar.hiring_manager_in_depth_review — Hiring Manager In-Depth Review

Detailed evaluation of candidate seniority, project ownership history, trade-off reasoning, and team-specific mission fit.

- Stage: hiring-manager · Order: 9 · Passes when: The hiring manager confirms the required depth and approves the candidate for the final panel.
- Precedes: bar.team_cross_functional_panel

### bar.team_cross_functional_panel — Team & Cross-Functional Panel

Multi-interviewer round assessing collaborative problem solving, code review etiquette, cross-functional communication, and cultural norms.

- Stage: team · Order: 10 · Passes when: Consensus score among team panelists meets or exceeds hire recommendation threshold.
- Precedes: bar.compensation_levelling_reconciliation

### bar.compensation_levelling_reconciliation — Compensation & Levelling Reconciliation

Internal alignment between candidate expected compensation/level and company pay bands / levelling grid.

- Stage: compensation · Order: 11 · Passes when: Candidate expectations fit within approved salary band and equity guidelines for the target grade.
- Precedes: bar.headcount_executive_budget_approval

### bar.headcount_executive_budget_approval — Headcount & Executive Budget Approval

Formal sign-off by department leadership, finance, and talent committee to commit budget for the written offer.

- Stage: offer · Order: 12 · Passes when: Active headcount requisition is formally certified and unblocked by financial leadership.
- Precedes: bar.reference_background_verification

### bar.reference_background_verification — Reference & Background Verification

Third-party or internal verification of past employment records, academic degrees, and professional references.

- Stage: post-offer · Order: 13 · Passes when: All mandatory background checks clear with no unresolved factual discrepancies.
- Precedes: bar.offer_closing_contract_execution

### bar.offer_closing_contract_execution — Offer Closing & Contract Execution

Final mutual execution of the formal employment agreement and start-date confirmation.

- Stage: post-offer · Order: 14 · Passes when: Both parties sign offer contract and onboarding workflow is triggered.

### bar.client_profile_approval_and_client_interview — Client Profile Approval and Client Interview

The candidate profile is submitted to the end client for review, followed by a client-side interview round.

- Stage: client · Order: 15 · Passes when: The client approves the profile submission and signs off on the technical and culture match after the interview.

### bar.probation_period_post_start_confirmation — Probation Period & Post-Start Confirmation

The post-hire evaluation interval (statutory or contractual probation) during which performance, delivery, and team alignment are formally confirmed.

- Stage: post-offer · Order: 16 · Passes when: The applicable probation interval ends without a valid probation-based termination, and employment continues under the governing contract and law.

## Mechanisms

### mech.ats_parser_extraction_failure — ATS Parser Extraction Failure

Multi-column formatting, graphics, custom fonts, or unsupported document layouts cause ATS parser to corrupt or omit critical work history.

- Actor: system · Nature: noise · Visibility: inferable · Removability: candidate
- Operates at: bar.application_ingestion, bar.automated_filter_parser_threshold
- Emits: obs.complete_silence_after_submission (void), obs.rejection_within_minutes_of_application_submission (direct)
- Does NOT establish: Does not imply human recruiter evaluated and disliked candidate experience.

### mech.automated_application_expiration_timeout — Automated Application Expiration Timeout

The ATS is configured to reject in bulk every application still pending after 45 or 60 days.

- Actor: system · Nature: rule · Visibility: opaque · Removability: none
- Operates at: bar.application_ingestion, bar.inbound_screening_triage
- Emits: obs.rejection_after_the_application_sat_pending_for_months (direct), obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (void), obs.complete_silence_after_submission (void)
- Does NOT establish: A bulk timeout rejection carries no assessment of the profile at all.

### mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter — Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter

Deterministic filter rejecting applications missing exact acronyms, certifications, or specific years-of-experience thresholds.

- Actor: system · Nature: rule · Visibility: inferable · Removability: candidate
- Operates at: bar.automated_filter_parser_threshold
- Emits: obs.rejection_within_minutes_of_application_submission (direct), obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (euphemism)
- Does NOT establish: Passing keyword filters does not guarantee interview invitation.

### mech.bench_priority_fill — Bench-Priority Fill

An engineer already employed and between projects becomes available mid-search, and the seat the external candidate is interviewing for is filled from the bench.

- Actor: policy · Nature: incentive · Visibility: opaque · Removability: none
- Operates at: bar.requisition_approval_public_posting, bar.inbound_screening_triage · honest baseline
- Emits: obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (euphemism), obs.position_closed_after_final_interview_without_hire (void), obs.rejection_naming_an_internal_hire_as_the_outcome (direct)
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the internal candidate was earmarked before the search was published — that is mech.pre_selected_internal_candidate, and from the outside the two are the same.
- Does NOT establish: Does not mean the external assessment found the candidate short: the search can end for reasons that never reached the assessment.

### mech.bid_conditional_talent_pool — Bid-Conditional Talent Pool

Recruiters run a real search for a real role whose funding depends on a contract that is not yet signed; if the bid is lost, the pool is closed without the role ever having existed.

- Actor: recruiter · Nature: incentive · Visibility: opaque · Removability: none
- Operates at: bar.outbound_sourcing_talent_pool_contact
- Emits: obs.complete_silence_after_submission (void), obs.unsolicited_recruiter_outreach_followed_by_ghosting (void), obs.republished_job_posting_with_refreshed_date_and_identical_requirement_body (distortion)
- Does NOT establish: Does not mean the role was fake: it was real and conditional, which is a different structure from a posting nobody intends to fill.
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the recruiter was free to disclose the bid's existence.

### mech.communication_or_working_style_friction — Communication or Working Style Friction

During a collaborative interview exercise the candidate is abrasive in tone, defensive about critique, or not listening.

- Actor: candidate · Nature: bias · Visibility: observable · Removability: candidate
- Operates at: bar.recruiter_screening_call, bar.team_cross_functional_panel · honest baseline
- Emits: obs.communication_mismatch_or_tone_friction_in_panel (direct), obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (euphemism)
- Does NOT establish: Style friction in a high-pressure interview is not a permanent personality defect.

### mech.domain_specificity_over_weighting — Domain Specificity Over-Weighting

The interviewer holds experience in one exact vertical — adtech, crypto, a named payment processor — as a requirement, ahead of transferable systems depth.

- Actor: hiring-manager · Nature: bias · Visibility: inferable · Removability: intermediary
- Operates at: bar.recruiter_screening_call, bar.hiring_manager_in_depth_review
- Emits: obs.rejection_naming_a_specific_industry_sector_as_required (direct), obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (euphemism), obs.explicit_feedback_citing_skill_depth_shortfall (direct)
- Does NOT establish: Transferable general engineering skills are not disproven by lack of specific proprietary protocol knowledge.

### mech.employment_gap_downranking_bias — Employment Gap Downranking Bias

Automated ranking algorithms or human screeners discount candidates with recent career breaks regardless of verified project history.

- Actor: system · Nature: bias · Visibility: inferable · Removability: none
- Operates at: bar.automated_filter_parser_threshold, bar.inbound_screening_triage
- Emits: obs.complete_silence_after_submission (void), obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (euphemism)
- Does NOT establish: An employment gap does not correlate with a decline in technical ability.

### mech.experience_age_grading_mismatch — Experience-Age Grading Mismatch

A candidate with 10+ years applies for a role graded at mid or senior, and the screening note records forecasts about boredom, short tenure and salary expectation.

- Actor: recruiter · Nature: bias · Visibility: inferable · Removability: none
- Operates at: bar.inbound_screening_triage, bar.recruiter_screening_call, bar.hiring_manager_in_depth_review
- Emits: obs.feedback_stating_candidate_is_overqualified_for_the_grade (direct), obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (euphemism)
- Does NOT establish: Being rejected as "overqualified" is an organisational tier mismatch, not a candidate deficiency.

### mech.genuine_technical_skill_shortfall — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

The candidate’s verified technical execution or domain depth does not meet the established baseline for the role level.

- Actor: candidate · Nature: rule · Visibility: inferable · Removability: candidate
- Operates at: bar.technical_screen_live_assessment, bar.take_home_work_sample_evaluation, bar.hiring_manager_in_depth_review · honest baseline
- Emits: obs.explicit_feedback_citing_skill_depth_shortfall (direct), obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (euphemism)
- Does NOT establish: Rejection does not mean the candidate has no engineering ability, only that the requirement bar was unmet for this specific benchmark.

### mech.headcount_freeze_or_budget_cancellation — Headcount Freeze or Budget Cancellation

Executive leadership or finance halts all new hires across division due to macroeconomic factors or revenue shifts mid-interview process.

- Actor: policy · Nature: rule · Visibility: inferable · Removability: none
- Operates at: bar.team_cross_functional_panel, bar.headcount_executive_budget_approval, bar.offer_closing_contract_execution
- Emits: obs.position_closed_after_final_interview_without_hire (direct), obs.offer_rescinded_or_delayed_due_to_internal_freeze (direct)
- Does NOT establish: Candidate performance in interview was not the causal trigger for process termination.

### mech.hidden_evaluation_rubric_or_undisclosed_priority — Hidden Evaluation Rubric or Undisclosed Priority

The panel grades the candidate against architectural preferences, internal frameworks and house conventions that were not stated in the posting or in the round.

- Actor: hiring-manager · Nature: bias · Visibility: opaque · Removability: intermediary
- Operates at: bar.technical_screen_live_assessment, bar.hiring_manager_in_depth_review, bar.team_cross_functional_panel
- Emits: obs.explicit_feedback_citing_skill_depth_shortfall (distortion), obs.conflicting_feedback_across_different_interviewers (direct)
- Does NOT establish: Not guessing an unstated preference is not a shortfall in core competence.

### mech.hiring_manager_consensus_impasse — Hiring Manager Consensus Impasse

The panel splits evenly, no one holds a tiebreaking vote, and the rule for the absence of consensus is no hire.

- Actor: hiring-manager · Nature: bias · Visibility: opaque · Removability: none
- Operates at: bar.team_cross_functional_panel
- Emits: obs.conflicting_feedback_across_different_interviewers (direct), obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (euphemism)
- Does NOT establish: A split panel reflects the absence of a calibrated internal bar, not a failure by the candidate.

### mech.inflated_requisition_requirements_vs_actual_team_needs — Inflated Requisition Requirements vs Actual Team Needs

The posting lists 10+ named technologies and a Staff-level bar for a role whose actual work is feature delivery.

- Actor: hiring-manager · Nature: incentive · Visibility: inferable · Removability: intermediary
- Operates at: bar.requisition_approval_public_posting, bar.automated_filter_parser_threshold, bar.recruiter_screening_call
- Emits: obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (euphemism), obs.materially_similar_role_reposted_shortly_after_rejection (noise)
- Does NOT establish: Failing to meet an inflated "wishlist" does not establish anything about how the candidate would do the team's actual work.

### mech.interview_resource_scheduling_saturation — Interview Resource & Scheduling Saturation

Engineering interviewers carry sprint commitments alongside the panels they sit on, and rounds are moved, read cold, or dropped.

- Actor: hiring-manager · Nature: noise · Visibility: inferable · Removability: intermediary
- Operates at: bar.technical_screen_live_assessment, bar.hiring_manager_in_depth_review, bar.team_cross_functional_panel
- Emits: obs.multiple_interview_reschedulings_or_interviewer_no_show (direct), obs.complete_silence_after_submission (noise)
- Does NOT establish: Rescheduling is an operational fact and does not indicate a negative evaluation.

### mech.location_or_timezone_compliance_constraint — Location or Timezone Compliance Constraint

The company has no legal entity or provider that can issue an employment contract in the jurisdiction where the candidate resides.

- Actor: policy · Nature: rule · Visibility: observable · Removability: intermediary
- Operates at: bar.automated_filter_parser_threshold, bar.recruiter_screening_call
- Emits: obs.rejection_naming_a_jurisdiction_or_work_eligibility_ground (direct), obs.rejection_within_minutes_of_application_submission (direct), obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (euphemism)
- Does NOT establish: The jurisdictional barrier is entirely independent of the candidate's technical competence.

### mech.mid_process_role_requirement_redefinition — Mid-Process Role Requirement Redefinition

The team changes the stack, the seniority level or the project scope while candidates are mid-process, and the assessments already taken no longer apply.

- Actor: hiring-manager · Nature: noise · Visibility: inferable · Removability: none
- Operates at: bar.hiring_manager_in_depth_review, bar.team_cross_functional_panel, bar.compensation_levelling_reconciliation
- Emits: obs.position_closed_after_final_interview_without_hire (distortion), obs.materially_similar_role_reposted_shortly_after_rejection (direct)
- Does NOT establish: The rejection was driven by a shift in the team's mandate, not by the candidate's interview answers.

### mech.portfolio_work_artifact_misinterpretation — Portfolio / Work Artifact Misinterpretation

The surface a screener opens does not show the candidate's architecture work, which sits in a non-standard repository layout or in contributions under another organisation.

- Actor: candidate · Nature: noise · Visibility: inferable · Removability: candidate
- Operates at: bar.inbound_screening_triage, bar.technical_screen_live_assessment
- Emits: obs.feedback_naming_as_absent_something_the_submitted_work_contains (direct), obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (euphemism), obs.explicit_feedback_citing_skill_depth_shortfall (distortion)
- Does NOT establish: Misinterpreted architecture can be corrected through structured documentation.

### mech.pre_selected_internal_candidate — Pre-Selected Internal Candidate

Requisition was publicly advertised to satisfy corporate policy or legal compliance while an internal employee was already earmarked for the role.

- Actor: policy · Nature: incentive · Visibility: opaque · Removability: none
- Operates at: bar.requisition_approval_public_posting, bar.application_ingestion, bar.inbound_screening_triage, bar.hiring_manager_in_depth_review
- Emits: obs.rejection_naming_an_internal_hire_as_the_outcome (direct), obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (euphemism), obs.position_closed_after_final_interview_without_hire (euphemism)
- Does NOT establish: Cannot be asserted as fact without internal hiring log confirmation.

### mech.probation_used_as_extended_de_facto_interview — Probation Used as Extended De-Facto Interview

An employer may rely on probation as an additional selection stage, using on-the-job assessment to resolve uncertainty that the interview process left open.

- Actor: hiring-manager · Nature: incentive · Visibility: inferable · Removability: intermediary
- Operates at: bar.probation_period_post_start_confirmation
- Emits: obs.offer_accepted_followed_by_delayed_start_date_or_post_signing_revocation (direct), obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (euphemism), obs.rejection_naming_an_internal_hire_as_the_outcome (noise)
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the employee committed gross misconduct.
- Does NOT establish: Probation rules define legal boundaries; they do not establish that employers systematically lower interview thresholds or use probation as a filtering strategy.

### mech.recruiter_volume_quota_incentive_distortion — Recruiter Volume & Quota Incentive Distortion

Applicant volume (500+ per req) runs past the screening hours available; profiles are read at the speed of the queue and matched against the pattern the requisition was described with.

- Actor: recruiter · Nature: incentive · Visibility: inferable · Removability: intermediary
- Operates at: bar.inbound_screening_triage, bar.recruiter_screening_call
- Emits: obs.complete_silence_after_submission (void), obs.unsolicited_recruiter_outreach_followed_by_ghosting (noise)
- Does NOT establish: Does not mean the recruiter is individually negligent; the capacity mismatch is structural.

### mech.reference_check_discrepancy_or_regulatory_ineligibility — Reference Check Discrepancy or Regulatory Ineligibility

A third-party check returns employment dates it could not verify, a degree the registrar has not confirmed, or a prior engagement flagged as a conflict of interest.

- Actor: candidate · Nature: rule · Visibility: observable · Removability: candidate
- Operates at: bar.reference_background_verification · honest baseline
- Emits: obs.offer_rescinded_or_delayed_due_to_internal_freeze (direct), obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (euphemism)
- Does NOT establish: An administrative mismatch in dates is distinct from fraudulent misrepresentation on a CV.

### mech.speculative_sourcing_talent_pooling_without_opening — Speculative Sourcing / Talent Pooling Without Opening

Recruiters open conversations and build candidate pools against headcount that has not been approved or funded.

- Actor: recruiter · Nature: incentive · Visibility: opaque · Removability: none
- Operates at: bar.requisition_approval_public_posting, bar.outbound_sourcing_talent_pool_contact, bar.inbound_screening_triage, bar.recruiter_screening_call
- Emits: obs.unsolicited_recruiter_outreach_followed_by_ghosting (distortion), obs.complete_silence_after_submission (void), obs.republished_job_posting_with_refreshed_date_and_identical_requirement_body (distortion)
- Does NOT establish: Ghosting after an outbound message indicates the absence of an immediate opening, not a rejection of the profile.

### mech.stale_or_orphaned_job_requisition — Stale or Orphaned Job Requisition

Job posting remains active on careers page and aggregator portals despite the team having ceased active hiring or closed headcount.

- Actor: system · Nature: void · Visibility: opaque · Removability: none
- Operates at: bar.requisition_approval_public_posting, bar.application_ingestion, bar.automated_filter_parser_threshold, bar.inbound_screening_triage
- Emits: obs.complete_silence_after_submission (void), obs.materially_similar_role_reposted_shortly_after_rejection (noise), obs.republished_job_posting_with_refreshed_date_and_identical_requirement_body (distortion)
- Does NOT establish: Application silence does not reflect candidate suitability.

### mech.start_date_slippage_and_post_acceptance_revocation — Start-Date Slippage and Post-Acceptance Revocation

A budgeting or project-authorisation change can lead an employer to defer a confirmed start date or withdraw an accepted offer between signing and day one.

- Actor: policy · Nature: incentive · Visibility: opaque · Removability: none
- Operates at: bar.offer_closing_contract_execution, bar.probation_period_post_start_confirmation
- Emits: obs.offer_accepted_followed_by_delayed_start_date_or_post_signing_revocation (direct), obs.complete_silence_after_submission (void), obs.offer_rescinded_or_delayed_due_to_internal_freeze (euphemism)
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that candidate credentials or references failed validation.
- Does NOT establish: The linked UK guidance establishes potential legal consequences of withdrawal, not the employer's motive or the frequency of this mechanism.

### mech.stronger_competing_candidate_in_final_cohort — Stronger Competing Candidate in Final Cohort

Candidate cleared all passing bars, but another applicant in the same pipeline demonstrated superior domain overlap or lower onboarding overhead.

- Actor: candidate · Nature: rule · Visibility: opaque · Removability: none
- Operates at: bar.hiring_manager_in_depth_review, bar.team_cross_functional_panel, bar.headcount_executive_budget_approval · honest baseline
- Emits: obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (euphemism), obs.position_closed_after_final_interview_without_hire (distortion)
- Does NOT establish: Does not mean candidate had negative feedback; relative cohort ranking is outside candidate control.

### mech.take_home_evaluation_fatigue_asymmetry — Take-Home Evaluation Fatigue & Asymmetry

A 15-hour take-home is reviewed in minutes, and the structure and tests held outside the files that were opened do not reach the assessment.

- Actor: hiring-manager · Nature: noise · Visibility: opaque · Removability: none
- Operates at: bar.take_home_work_sample_evaluation
- Emits: obs.take_home_assignment_exceeding_reasonable_stated_scope (noise), obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (euphemism)
- Does NOT establish: A take-home rejection made under evaluation fatigue does not measure the engineering in the submission.

### mech.unstated_compensation_band_discrepancy — Unstated Compensation Band Discrepancy

Candidate market rate exceeds budgeted compensation for the requisition, but salary band was never published or clarified early.

- Actor: policy · Nature: rule · Visibility: opaque · Removability: intermediary
- Operates at: bar.recruiter_screening_call, bar.compensation_levelling_reconciliation
- Emits: obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template (euphemism), obs.compensation_band_reduced_or_altered_mid_process (direct), obs.feedback_stating_candidate_is_overqualified_for_the_grade (euphemism)
- Does NOT establish: Rejection does not mean candidate is overpriced for the market, only mismatched with this specific employer budget.

## Patterns

### pat.closed_then_reposted_requisition_motif — Closed-Then-Reposted Requisition Motif

A candidate completes multiple late-stage interviews, is rejected with a generic message, and sees the identical role reposted weeks later.

- Triggers when: The role is closed and the candidate rejected, and a materially similar listing is publicly reopened within 60 days.
- Requires: obs.position_closed_after_final_interview_without_hire, obs.materially_similar_role_reposted_shortly_after_rejection · Mechanisms: mech.stronger_competing_candidate_in_final_cohort, mech.stale_or_orphaned_job_requisition, mech.hidden_evaluation_rubric_or_undisclosed_priority, mech.mid_process_role_requirement_redefinition
- Establishes: The prior process ended without placing this candidate, and a materially similar public listing appeared within the stated interval.
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the original job listing was fake or a ghost job.
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the candidate was intentionally misled.

### pat.compensation_double_bind — Compensation Double Bind

The candidate has to name a compensation expectation first: a high number ends the process, and a low one lowers the level the candidate is assessed at.

- Triggers when: The candidate is asked for a compensation number before the band for the role is stated, and the band is not stated in return.
- Requires: obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template, obs.compensation_band_reduced_or_altered_mid_process · Mechanisms: mech.unstated_compensation_band_discrepancy, mech.experience_age_grading_mismatch
- Establishes: The candidate's compensation number was requested before the role's band was disclosed, creating an information asymmetry at that point in the process.
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the employer has an unlimited budget, or that any of this is malicious.

### pat.experience_age_impossibility — Experience-Age Impossibility

A requisition requires more years of hands-on experience with a specific framework or tool than that technology has existed in the open-source ecosystem.

- Triggers when: Job description or automated screen requires X years of experience where X > technology_age.
- Requires: obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template, obs.rejection_within_minutes_of_application_submission · Mechanisms: mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter, mech.inflated_requisition_requirements_vs_actual_team_needs
- Establishes: The published numeric requirement exceeds the technology's age; if an ATS log shows the same threshold running, the impossible requirement was also operational.
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish who authored or reviewed the requirement, or that it caused a rejection unless an operational rule or decision record confirms that link.

### pat.seniority_double_bind — Seniority Double Bind

The same candidate is rejected as overqualified for junior and mid-level roles and as underqualified, or not specialised enough, for staff and leadership roles.

- Triggers when: The candidate is rejected as overqualified at level N and as short on depth at level N+1 within the same market cycle.
- Requires: obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template, obs.feedback_stating_candidate_is_overqualified_for_the_grade · Mechanisms: mech.genuine_technical_skill_shortfall, mech.unstated_compensation_band_discrepancy, mech.experience_age_grading_mismatch
- Establishes: Within one market cycle, the candidate received stated outcomes placing them above one level and below the adjacent level.
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish that the candidate lacks market value.
- Does NOT establish: Does not establish malice or coordinated collusion between employers.

## Loops

### loop.employment_gap_penalty_loop — Employment Gap Penalty Loop

An employment gap triggers automated downranking (mech.employment_gap_downranking_bias), which pushes the profile below keyword and qualification filters (mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter); fewer interview invitations lengthen the gap, which in turn strengthens the downranking.

- mech.employment_gap_downranking_bias amplifies mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter
- mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter amplifies mech.employment_gap_downranking_bias

### loop.inflated_requirements_search_saturation_loop — Inflated-Requirements Search Saturation Loop

Teams write inflated requirements that filter out strong generalists; the search stays open for months, recruiters tire of it, and the role is redefined mid-process.

- mech.inflated_requisition_requirements_vs_actual_team_needs amplifies mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter
- mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter amplifies mech.mid_process_role_requirement_redefinition
- mech.mid_process_role_requirement_redefinition amplifies mech.inflated_requisition_requirements_vs_actual_team_needs

### loop.take_home_opportunity_cost_saturation_loop — Take-Home Opportunity-Cost Saturation Loop

Candidates spend heavy hours on take-home assignments with no bounded scope, which leaves less time for applications, while reviewers work through the queue under evaluation fatigue.

- mech.interview_resource_scheduling_saturation amplifies mech.take_home_evaluation_fatigue_asymmetry
- mech.take_home_evaluation_fatigue_asymmetry amplifies mech.interview_resource_scheduling_saturation

## Interventions

### int.a_named_decider_and_a_written_rule_for_a_split_panel — A named decider and a written rule for a split panel

Before the panel sits, one member is named as holding the decision and the rule for an even split is written down; when the split happens, the candidate is told that it did and which way the rule ran.

- Actor: hiring-manager · Scope: team · Cost: low
- Targets: mech.hiring_manager_consensus_impasse, bar.team_cross_functional_panel
- Expected: mech.hiring_manager_consensus_impasse keeps operating — panels will split — but stops resolving by default and unrecorded
- Expected: The candidate learns the outcome turned on a tie rule, not on a finding about them

### int.auto_close_stale_job_requisitions — Auto-Close Stale Job Requisitions

Implement an automated ATS policy to expire public listings when headcount authorisation lapses or the configured interview-inactivity interval elapses.

- Actor: employer-policy · Scope: organizational · Cost: low
- Targets: mech.stale_or_orphaned_job_requisition, bar.application_ingestion, pat.closed_then_reposted_requisition_motif, loop.inflated_requirements_search_saturation_loop
- Expected: mech.stale_or_orphaned_job_requisition stops operating: a listing cannot outlive the authorisation that funded it
- Expected: Silence after applying acquires a bound — the record is closed and the closure is sent

### int.bench_availability_declared_at_each_stage_gate — Bench availability declared at each stage gate

At every advance the search states whether an already-employed engineer between projects could still take the seat, and an external candidate closed out by a bench fill is told so, with the date the availability appeared.

- Actor: employer-policy · Scope: organizational · Cost: low
- Targets: mech.bench_priority_fill, bar.requisition_approval_public_posting, bar.inbound_screening_triage
- Expected: mech.bench_priority_fill keeps operating — it cannot be removed — but stops being read as a verdict on the candidate
- Expected: External effort spent against an internally contestable seat becomes countable, and can be priced

### int.candidate_ats_parser_conformance_test_utility — Candidate ATS Parser Conformance Test Utility

Provide candidates with an open-source parsing validation tool to verify CV machine-readability before submission.

- Actor: candidate-action · Scope: individual · Cost: low
- Targets: mech.ats_parser_extraction_failure, bar.automated_filter_parser_threshold, pat.experience_age_impossibility
- Expected: The candidate can see the extraction before submitting, so an unreadable file is distinguishable from a thin one
- Expected: mech.ats_parser_extraction_failure moves from invisible to checkable on the candidate's side of the line

### int.candidate_work_index_submitted_with_the_application — Candidate Work Index Submitted With the Application

Submit a one-page index naming each work artefact, the part of it that is the candidate's and the direct path to it, and open that index in the first minutes of the live screen.

- Actor: candidate-action · Scope: individual · Cost: low
- Targets: mech.portfolio_work_artifact_misinterpretation, bar.technical_screen_live_assessment, bar.inbound_screening_triage
- Expected: mech.portfolio_work_artifact_misinterpretation loses its default: the surface opened is the one the candidate named, with the part that is theirs stated on it
- Expected: A contribution held under another organisation arrives as a commit range rather than as something to be discovered
- Expected: The index travels with the application, so bar.inbound_screening_triage and bar.technical_screen_live_assessment open the same named artefacts instead of whatever a profile page shows first

### int.contractable_jurisdictions_listed_in_the_posting — Contractable jurisdictions listed in the posting

The posting names the countries in which the employer can actually issue a contract — through an entity, an employer of record, or a contractor arrangement — so a constraint that no interview can change is known before the first call.

- Actor: employer-policy · Scope: organizational · Cost: low
- Targets: mech.location_or_timezone_compliance_constraint, bar.automated_filter_parser_threshold, bar.recruiter_screening_call
- Expected: mech.location_or_timezone_compliance_constraint stops being discovered at the offer stage
- Expected: A lawful contracting limit becomes distinguishable from a ground that is not one

### int.critique_injected_on_script_in_the_collaborative_exercise — Critique injected on script in the collaborative exercise

The collaborative round carries a written script: the same objection is raised at the same point for every candidate, and the panel records what was said in response rather than how the room felt.

- Actor: hiring-manager · Scope: team · Cost: low
- Targets: mech.communication_or_working_style_friction, bar.recruiter_screening_call, bar.team_cross_functional_panel
- Expected: mech.communication_or_working_style_friction is measured against a common prompt rather than inferred from an interviewer's chosen one
- Expected: Interviewer variance stops entering the verdict as if it were candidate behaviour

### int.dated_funding_certification_before_the_final_round — Dated Funding Certification Before the Final Round

Carry a funding-certified-through date on every requisition, refuse to schedule a final round unless that date covers the expected start, and release the countersignature on a live certification rather than on a second approval.

- Actor: employer-policy · Scope: organizational · Cost: medium
- Targets: bar.headcount_executive_budget_approval, bar.offer_closing_contract_execution, mech.headcount_freeze_or_budget_cancellation
- Expected: bar.headcount_executive_budget_approval is passed before the final round is scheduled: the certification date is in the requisition before the panel sits, rather than after it recommends
- Expected: mech.headcount_freeze_or_budget_cancellation meets a requisition whose funded-through date is either live or lapsed; where a freeze lands mid-loop the requisition changes to a dated state and every candidate in flight is written to on that date
- Expected: bar.offer_closing_contract_execution stops carrying a funding decision: the countersignature is blocked while the certification has lapsed and released while it is live

### int.disqualifying_criteria_published_with_the_posting — Disqualifying criteria published with the posting

Every criterion the automated filter can reject on — a required acronym, a named certification, a years-of-experience threshold — is listed in the posting as a disqualifier, so a deterministic gate is legible before the application is written.

- Actor: employer-policy · Scope: organizational · Cost: low
- Targets: mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter, bar.automated_filter_parser_threshold
- Expected: mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter stops operating unseen: the rule that rejects is the rule that was published
- Expected: An application withheld against a stated disqualifier costs neither side a review

### int.distinct_closure_status_for_unreviewed_applications — Distinct Closure Status for Unreviewed Applications

Give the ATS a terminal status for an application closed without a human opening it, distinct from the one used for a reviewed decline, bind it into the notification template, and count it on the requisition.

- Actor: ats-vendor · Scope: ecosystem · Cost: medium
- Targets: bar.inbound_screening_triage, mech.recruiter_volume_quota_incentive_distortion, mech.automated_application_expiration_timeout
- Expected: mech.automated_application_expiration_timeout can no longer write the value used for a decision: the expiry job writes closed_unreviewed, and the notification template carries that status
- Expected: The gap mech.recruiter_volume_quota_incentive_distortion runs on becomes a figure on the requisition — applications closed unopened are counted where applications received already are
- Expected: bar.inbound_screening_triage leaves a state that can be read from outside: not reached, reviewed and not advanced, or closed with the search

### int.domain_requirement_carries_a_stated_ramp_time — Domain requirement carries a stated ramp time

A requisition that asks for experience in one named vertical must state how long the team believes that domain takes to learn; where the answer is weeks, the requirement is scored as a preference rather than a gate.

- Actor: hiring-manager · Scope: team · Cost: low
- Targets: mech.domain_specificity_over_weighting, bar.recruiter_screening_call, bar.hiring_manager_in_depth_review
- Expected: mech.domain_specificity_over_weighting must state its own cost before it can reject
- Expected: A requirement assembled from something other than the work becomes visible at the point it is written

### int.internal_candidacy_stated_in_the_posting — Internal Candidacy Stated in the Posting

Where a formal internal candidacy exists against a requisition at the moment it is published, the posting says so and says what the external loop decides.

- Actor: employer-policy · Scope: organizational · Cost: medium
- Targets: mech.pre_selected_internal_candidate, bar.requisition_approval_public_posting
- Expected: mech.pre_selected_internal_candidate stops being opaque at the gate it operates at: the composition of the slate is stated where the posting is, not at minute 41 of a final round
- Expected: bar.requisition_approval_public_posting publishes one more field — whether the external loop runs against an internal candidacy already formally under consideration

### int.interview_seats_booked_with_prep_time_and_a_second_name_on_the_rota — Interview Seats Booked With Prep Time and a Second Name on the Rota

Book every interview seat as preparation plus session, take those hours off the sprint board, and give each round a second name on a standing rota so an unavailable interviewer passes the seat rather than moves the date.

- Actor: hiring-manager · Scope: team · Cost: medium
- Targets: mech.interview_resource_scheduling_saturation, bar.technical_screen_live_assessment
- Expected: mech.interview_resource_scheduling_saturation loses one of its two outputs: a seat that cannot be filled moves the seat, not the date
- Expected: A round at bar.technical_screen_live_assessment is booked with reading time attached to it, so the material is opened before the session or the seat passes to the second name
- Expected: Interviewer hours sit on the sprint board as committed work rather than as an overrun absorbed by whoever had the slot

### int.outreach_states_the_requisition_behind_it — Outreach States the Requisition Behind It

Every outbound message names the requisition it is sent against and its state — approved and open, or a pool record against a forecast — and the pool records opened against a forecast are answered on the day planning decides it.

- Actor: recruiter-process · Scope: organizational · Cost: low
- Targets: bar.outbound_sourcing_talent_pool_contact, mech.speculative_sourcing_talent_pooling_without_opening, mech.bid_conditional_talent_pool
- Expected: bar.outbound_sourcing_talent_pool_contact's pass condition is stated in the first message: whether a reply attaches to an authorised requisition or to a pool is part of what is sent
- Expected: mech.speculative_sourcing_talent_pooling_without_opening becomes datable — a conversation held against an unapproved forecast carries the planning date it depends on
- Expected: The silence after a speculative conversation acquires a bound: the planning decision goes to the records opened against that forecast

### int.publish_the_technical_screen_s_columns_and_threshold_before_the_round — Publish the Technical Screen's Columns and Threshold Before the Round

Publish the columns, their weights and the advancing threshold of the live technical screen alongside the posting, and score the round on those columns.

- Actor: employer-policy · Scope: organizational · Cost: medium
- Targets: bar.technical_screen_live_assessment, mech.interview_resource_scheduling_saturation
- Expected: bar.technical_screen_live_assessment's instrument exists before the hour it scores: the columns, the weights and the line are readable from outside the panel
- Expected: A total one point under the threshold at bar.technical_screen_live_assessment is locatable, because the number it is compared with is published
- Expected: A round read cold under mech.interview_resource_scheduling_saturation is scored on the published columns rather than on what the hour left as an impression

### int.recorded_finalist_standing_with_a_dated_re_entry_route — Recorded Finalist Standing With a Dated Re-Entry Route

Record, for every finalist who cleared the bar and received no offer, the cohort size, the class of reason and a dated stage the record re-enters at when a requisition at the same level opens.

- Actor: recruiter-process · Scope: organizational · Cost: low
- Targets: mech.stronger_competing_candidate_in_final_cohort, bar.headcount_executive_budget_approval, pat.closed_then_reposted_requisition_motif
- Expected: mech.stronger_competing_candidate_in_final_cohort becomes a recorded outcome: the cohort size and the class of reason sit in the record and in what is sent, instead of arriving as a decline with no account of the group
- Expected: bar.headcount_executive_budget_approval: a requisition that closes with more finalists than offers leaves standings behind it that outlast the closing
- Expected: pat.closed_then_reposted_requisition_motif: a reposted requisition matches against the standings recorded against its previous run, and the stage a matched record re-enters at is stated

### int.remove_career_gap_feature_from_automated_ranking_models — Remove Career Gap Feature from Automated Ranking Models

Disable employment duration gap penalties in recruitment AI algorithms and screening models.

- Actor: ats-vendor · Scope: ecosystem · Cost: low
- Targets: mech.employment_gap_downranking_bias, loop.employment_gap_penalty_loop
- Expected: mech.employment_gap_downranking_bias stops operating in the ranking model: continuity is no longer an input
- Expected: loop.employment_gap_penalty_loop loses the edge that closed it, because a gap can no longer widen the next gap

### int.requirement_changes_versioned_and_sent_to_candidates_in_flight — Requirement changes versioned and sent to candidates in flight

The requisition carries a dated version of its requirements; when the team changes the stack, the level or the scope mid-search, everyone in flight is told what changed and which of their completed assessments still counts.

- Actor: employer-policy · Scope: organizational · Cost: medium
- Targets: mech.mid_process_role_requirement_redefinition, bar.hiring_manager_in_depth_review, bar.team_cross_functional_panel
- Expected: mech.mid_process_role_requirement_redefinition keeps operating — needs change — but stops being absorbed silently by the candidate
- Expected: Which specification an assessment was taken against becomes a recorded fact rather than a later reinterpretation

### int.requirements_drawn_from_the_team_s_own_backlog — Requirements Drawn From the Team's Own Backlog

Draft the requisition's requirement list from the last two quarters of the team's actual work: every requirement the screen reads names a task it is required for, and anything without one is published in a separate section that is not screened on.

- Actor: hiring-manager · Scope: team · Cost: low
- Targets: mech.inflated_requisition_requirements_vs_actual_team_needs, bar.requisition_approval_public_posting, loop.inflated_requirements_search_saturation_loop
- Expected: mech.inflated_requisition_requirements_vs_actual_team_needs is split into two published lists: the screened list carries only requirements that name a task, and the wish sits in the section that is not screened on
- Expected: bar.requisition_approval_public_posting fixes a bar that states what each part of it is for: the requirement list is checkable against the team's own backlog rather than against the level in the grid
- Expected: loop.inflated_requirements_search_saturation_loop's entry point becomes an edit with a date — raising a requirement mid-search means adding a line with no task behind it

### int.screening_note_bound_to_observations_and_disposition_codes — Screening Note Bound to Observations and Disposition Codes

Restrict the screening note to the requirement, what the record shows and the surface opened, and close it with a fixed disposition code — including a referral to levelling for profiles above the graded band.

- Actor: recruiter-process · Scope: organizational · Cost: medium
- Targets: bar.inbound_screening_triage, mech.experience_age_grading_mismatch, mech.portfolio_work_artifact_misinterpretation
- Expected: The forecast mech.experience_age_grading_mismatch is recorded as has no field to sit in: the note takes the requirement, what the record shows, and a disposition code
- Expected: mech.portfolio_work_artifact_misinterpretation becomes checkable: the surface that was opened is recorded next to the note written from it, and the application form asks which surface that should be
- Expected: A profile above the graded band leaves bar.inbound_screening_triage with a routing code rather than a pass at screen

### int.standardized_late_stage_rejection_feedback_taxonomy — Standardized Late-Stage Rejection Feedback Taxonomy

Provide candidates reaching technical or panel stages with structured, rubric-based feedback categories rather than generic templates.

- Actor: recruiter-process · Scope: organizational · Cost: medium
- Targets: mech.genuine_technical_skill_shortfall, mech.hidden_evaluation_rubric_or_undisclosed_priority, bar.hiring_manager_in_depth_review, bar.team_cross_functional_panel, bar.client_profile_approval_and_client_interview, pat.seniority_double_bind, pat.closed_then_reposted_requisition_motif, loop.inflated_requirements_search_saturation_loop
- Expected: The stage and the criterion behind a late rejection become part of what is sent
- Expected: mech.hidden_evaluation_rubric_or_undisclosed_priority becomes checkable: a rubric that is reported has to exist before the round

### int.strict_take_home_timebox_blinded_evaluation_rubric — Strict Take-Home Timebox & Blinded Evaluation Rubric

Enforce strict 3-hour scope limits on take-homes, compensate candidates for extended samples, and grade submissions blind.

- Actor: hiring-manager · Scope: organizational · Cost: medium
- Targets: mech.take_home_evaluation_fatigue_asymmetry, loop.take_home_opportunity_cost_saturation_loop, bar.take_home_work_sample_evaluation
- Expected: mech.take_home_evaluation_fatigue_asymmetry loses its asymmetry: the timebox binds the reviewer as well as the candidate
- Expected: Who wrote a submission stops being an input to how it is scored

### int.upfront_compensation_band_disclosure — Upfront Compensation Band Disclosure

Publish verified salary and equity bands directly in job descriptions or disclose them prior to scheduling technical interview rounds.

- Actor: employer-policy · Scope: industry · Cost: low
- Targets: mech.unstated_compensation_band_discrepancy, bar.recruiter_screening_call, bar.compensation_levelling_reconciliation, pat.seniority_double_bind, pat.compensation_double_bind
- Expected: mech.unstated_compensation_band_discrepancy has nothing to operate on: the band is stated before the candidate is asked for a number
- Expected: bar.compensation_levelling_reconciliation becomes arithmetic rather than a negotiation about whether a band exists

### int.verification_discrepancy_disclosure_and_reconciliation_window — Verification Discrepancy Disclosure and Reconciliation Window

Classify every mandatory check in advance as reconcilable by document or disqualifying, release the disputed field and both values to the candidate on the day the result returns, and hold the offer open for a stated window with a revised start date.

- Actor: employer-policy · Scope: organizational · Cost: low
- Targets: bar.reference_background_verification, bar.probation_period_post_start_confirmation, mech.reference_check_discrepancy_or_regulatory_ineligibility, mech.start_date_slippage_and_post_acceptance_revocation, mech.probation_used_as_extended_de_facto_interview
- Expected: mech.reference_check_discrepancy_or_regulatory_ineligibility arrives as a named field with two values and a named closing document, instead of as a hold with no stated cause
- Expected: bar.reference_background_verification contains the reconciliation step: the window, the evidence that closes each check and who reviews it are set before the check runs rather than after it returns
- Expected: Which findings a document can close and which end the process is a published classification rather than a per-file decision

## Actors

### actor.ats_vendor — ATS vendor

The platform the funnel runs inside. Writes no policy and decides no hire, yet its defaults decide what a great many people ever see.

- Decides: What the parser can extract, and what it silently drops
- Decides: Which knockout rules a customer can configure, and which are on by default
- Decides: What the ranking model reads as a feature
- Decides: When an unreviewed application expires, and what it emails when it does
- Cannot see: Whether a rule its customer configured is lawful, reasonable or even intended
- Cannot see: What happened to a candidate outside the platform
- Cannot see: Whether the profile it scored 12/100 was unreadable rather than unqualified
- Measured on: Throughput and customer-visible efficiency, which are what the buyer evaluates
- Measured on: Feature parity with competitors, including features with known disparate effects
- Measured on: Defaults that reduce customer support load, not candidate confusion
- Could do (medium): Remove employment continuity from the ranking feature set — The feature set of the ranking model is written by the vendor, not configured per customer, so continuity is one of the few inputs here that no buyer has to agree to remove. While it stays in the set, a break in employment lowers the rank, a lower rank returns fewer interviews, and the next application carries a longer break. Costs: Every threshold customers tuned against the old score distribution shifts, and the field stays on competitors' feature lists after it leaves this one.
- Could do (medium): Stop scoring files the parser could not read — A file whose work history was lost in extraction and a file with no relevant work history reach the ranker as the same low number, and nothing downstream separates them. The extraction score is already computed, so routing anything below its threshold into a hold state rather than into the ranking is a change inside the pipeline the vendor owns. Costs: The hold state is work that lands on customers with nobody assigned to it, and the share of applications the platform disposes of without a person — a number the buyer is shown — falls.
- Could do (medium): Show the applicant the record the parser stored — The parsed record, not the uploaded file, is the version of the candidate every later stage reads, and it lives inside the platform rather than on the customer's careers page. Putting it into the submission confirmation with a way to correct it is the one point where the person who can tell that half the work history is missing is still able to say so. Costs: It creates a candidate-facing surface the vendor maintains and receives corrections through, used by people who are not the customer that bought the platform.
- Could do (medium): Hold the unreviewed queue instead of declining it — When the inactivity timeout fires, what it does and what it emails are the vendor's, and the same batch job can hold the applications and raise the requisition to the customer as having had no interview activity since a stated date. Whether the listing then comes down is a decision about funding, which is not visible from inside the platform. Holding rather than declining leaves that decision with the party who can make it, and leaves the applicants a state rather than a verdict. Costs: Every held queue becomes a customer decision the current default takes off their desk, and support load is exactly what these defaults are tuned to keep down.
- Could do (low): Show what a knockout rule removes before saving — Which knockout rules can be expressed, and what the configuration screen shows while one is being written, are both the vendor's. Whether a rule is reasonable is not visible from here; what it would have done to the applications already stored is, and running the draft against them puts that in front of the person who does hold the judgement. Costs: The dry run reads the customer's stored applications on the configuration path, and the screen now states a number the vendor stands behind — including when a draft rule would have ended the entire stored pool.
- Could do (medium): Name the rule and threshold in automated declines — The message an automated rule sends is the vendor's template, and the rule that fired, its threshold and the value it read are already in the log line behind it. Carrying those three items into the message is what separates a decline that names a criterion from one that arrives as a verdict on the person. Costs: The customer's configuration becomes quotable by everyone it is applied to, and a threshold stated in writing draws replies the current template does not.

### actor.candidate — Candidate

The person applying. The only party in the funnel who sees the whole of their own process and almost none of anyone else's.

- Decides: What is submitted, and in what machine-readable shape
- Decides: Which processes to enter and when to withdraw
- Decides: Which questions to ask, and when to ask them
- Decides: What is recorded: dates, wording, who said it
- Cannot see: Whether a requisition is funded, frozen or already promised internally
- Cannot see: The band, the level, and the rubric being scored against
- Cannot see: How many others are in the pipeline and where they came from
- Cannot see: Whether a rejection was written by a person or emitted by a rule
- Measured on: Reach a decision quickly enough to keep options open
- Measured on: Avoid spending unpaid hours on processes that were never live
- Measured on: Preserve the ability to reapply without having burned the relationship
- Could do (low): Check what the parser extracted before you submit — The shape of the file is on the candidate's side of the line; what a reader decides after it is not. A layout a person reads without difficulty can arrive in the record as zero work-history entries, and the score that follows is arithmetic on what was extracted. Running the file through a parser first turns an invisible failure into an edit. Costs: A single-column text export gives up the layout, and every later edit to the document has to be checked again.
- Could do (low): Ask what the conversation is attached to — Whether an approved requisition sits behind the outreach, and whether an internal candidacy is already running, are not in any field the candidate can see. Asking at the first exchange is the only route to either, and the answer arrives before the unpaid hours do. Costs: A logistics question in the first reply comes before any discussion of the work, and the answer cannot be checked against anything.
- Could do (medium): Ask for the band before any assessment is scheduled — The band, the level and the rubric are the second of the candidate's two lists, and the compensation bind runs on the candidate naming a number first. Asking for the band before an assessment is booked puts the mismatch at the screen rather than at week four, when the hours are already spent. Costs: The question can end a process at the screen, and stating an expectation early fixes a number before the level is fixed.
- Could do (low): Keep a dated record of every message — Dates, wording and who said it are the one part of the process the candidate holds in full. Kept as they arrive, they separate what a process established from what it did not: a rejection timed minutes after submission, a requisition back on the board, two rounds whose feedback disagrees. Costs: It is unpaid administrative time in the period when time is scarcest, and a complete record of a process that ends in silence is still a record of silence.
- Could do (medium): Submit at the stated timebox and name the cuts — The hours a work sample takes come out of the same budget as the search itself, and the minutes it is read for are set on the other side of the gate. Stopping at the stated timebox and writing down what was cut to fit it keeps the exercise inside the scope that was agreed and leaves the trade-offs on the page. Costs: A submission that stops at the timebox is read next to submissions that did not stop, and the reviewer's minutes are not something the candidate sets.
- Could do (medium): Set a date when a silent process closes — Silence after submission covers a listing nobody took down, a batch expiry job and a queue that was never reached, and none of the three is visible from outside. Choosing the closing date in advance turns an open question into a finished one and returns the hours to the searches that answered. Costs: An answer that arrives after the chosen date is treated as no answer, and the time already spent is written off rather than waited out.
