- US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, series JTU510000000000000LDL (Layoffs and discharges, information, total US, not seasonally adjusted).
- https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/JTU510000000000000LDL

### evidence.mean_vacancy_duration_information_sector_dhi_dfh — Mean vacancy duration, information sector (DHI-DFH)

The DHI-DFH measure reports the average number of working days taken to fill a vacant post, counting Monday to Saturday and excluding major holidays. For the information sector it stood at roughly 46 working days at the series' close in April 2018 — about seven and a half calendar weeks. An application still open six weeks after submission is therefore inside the ordinary life of a vacancy in this sector, not past it: the silence is what an open search looks like from outside, and its length alone carries no information about whether anyone has read the submission. The construction follows Davis, Faberman and Haltiwanger's method from the Quarterly Journal of Economics. It measures how long a vacancy stays open, never how long a rejection takes to arrive, and it says nothing about whether a given application was assessed at all. The series covers the US information sector from 2001 and was discontinued in 2018, so it describes the period up to that point and not the market since.

- DHI-DFH Mean Vacancy Duration Measure by Industry: Information (DHIDFHDMII), FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis; discontinued, last observation April 2018. Method per Davis, S. J., Faberman, R. J., & Haltiwanger, J. (2013). The Establishment-Level Behavior of Vacancies and Hiring. Quarterly Journal of Economics, 128(2).
- https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DHIDFHDMII

### evidence.naming_staff_for_a_contract_not_yet_won_is_an_adjudicated_practice — Naming staff for a contract not yet won is an adjudicated practice (GAO, ASRC Federal Data Solutions)

Hiring against unsigned funding is regular enough in US federal procurement to have its own body of decided law. To sustain a protest that an awardee performed an impermissible "bait and switch", GAO requires a protester to show "the awardee either knowingly or negligently represented that it would rely on specific personnel that it did not have a reasonable basis to expect to furnish during contract performance", that the agency relied on the misrepresentation, and that the reliance "had a material effect on the evaluation results". The test presupposes the practice it polices: bidders name real candidates for roles that exist only if the bid wins, and the mechanism is the contingent offer, which the decision distinguishes from an exclusive letter of commitment. What is adjudicated is the representation made to the agency, not what becomes of the candidate: the decision says nothing about whether anyone tells the candidate the funding is conditional, and nothing about what follows a lost bid. It governs US federal contracting and establishes that the arrangement is standard and regulated, not how often it occurs.

- ASRC Federal Data Solutions, LLC, B-421008.2; B-421008.3 (Comp. Gen. Dec. 2, 2022) (protest sustained). B-421008 is the original protest docket; the sustained decision carries the .2 and .3 numbers.
- https://www.gao.gov/products/b-421008,b-421008.2,b-421008.3

### evidence.nasdaq_composite_index_fred — NASDAQ Composite Index (FRED)

The NASDAQ Composite fell 36.4% from its record close of 16,057.44 on 19 November 2021 to its cycle low close of 10,213.29 on 28 December 2022.

- NASDAQ OMX Group, NASDAQ Composite Index [NASDAQCOM], retrieved from FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, 27 August 2026.
- https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/NASDAQCOM

### evidence.openings_that_exist_because_a_rule_requires_them_ukraine_civil_service_competitions — Openings that exist because a rule requires them (Ukraine, civil service competitions)

Ukrainian law requires a competition to fill a civil service post: "З метою добору осіб, здатних професійно виконувати посадові обов'язки, проводиться конкурс на зайняття посади державної служби". The requirement covers vacant posts, posts held during an absence, and category "А" posts whose term is expiring. Whole classes of publicly advertised openings therefore exist because a statute mandates the competition, not because an employer freely chose to search outside — so a public posting is not by itself evidence that the outcome is open. The law governs the Ukrainian civil service, not private technical hiring, and it says nothing about whether any particular competition has a favoured candidate; it establishes only that mandated-posting regimes exist and are ordinary.

- Закон України «Про державну службу» № 889-VIII, стаття 22 (Конкурс на зайняття посади державної служби).
- https://zakon.rada.gov.ua/laws/show/889-19

### evidence.pitchbook_nvca_venture_monitor_q4_2021 — PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor, Q4 2021

US venture-backed companies raised $329.6 billion in 2021, against a previous record of $166.6 billion in 2020. The report states the figures verbatim; they are data-provider estimates and are revised in later vintages.

- PitchBook Data and National Venture Capital Association, Q4 2021 PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor, 13 January 2022.
- https://nvca.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/Q4_2021_PitchBook_NVCA_Venture_Monitor.pdf

### evidence.pitchbook_nvca_venture_monitor_q4_2023 — PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor, Q4 2023

Every stage of the US private funding chain contracted at once. Deal value fell from $348.0 billion in 2021 to $170.6 billion in 2023. Exit value reached a decade low of $61.5 billion across an estimated 1,129 events. New fund commitments fell to a six-year low of $66.9 billion across 474 funds, against $169.2 billion in 2021 and $172.8 billion in 2022.

- PitchBook Data and National Venture Capital Association, Q4 2023 PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor, January 2024.
- https://nvca.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Q4-2023-PitchBook-NVCA-Venture-Monitor.pdf

### evidence.postings_without_a_fillable_requisition_measured_on_one_ats_platform_greenhouse — Postings without a fillable requisition, measured on one ATS platform (Greenhouse)

A hiring platform reports that in any given quarter 18–22% of the roles posted through it are classified by the vendor as postings not attached to a search that can be filled, and pairs this with a survey of 2,500 workers in the US, UK and Germany in which 61% said they had heard nothing after an interview. The first figure is the vendor's own classification of its own customers' postings and is not independently auditable; the second is a self-reported recollection, not a matched record. Together they establish that a posting's existence does not imply a live requisition behind it — not any proportion for the market as a whole.

- Greenhouse 2024 State of Job Hunting report. Platform classification of ghost jobs and survey of 2,500 workers across the US, UK and Germany.
- https://www.greenhouse.com/blog/greenhouse-2024-state-of-job-hunting-report

### evidence.pre_adverse_action_disclosure_in_employment_background_checks_15_u_s_c_1681b_b_3 — Pre-adverse-action disclosure in employment background checks (15 U.S.C. §1681b(b)(3))

Under US federal law, an employer intending to take adverse action based in whole or in part on a consumer report for employment purposes must first give the candidate a copy of the report and a written description of their rights. A narrower exception applies to specified transportation employment when the application was made by mail, telephone, computer, or a similar means: the required notice may follow within three business days of the action. The statute therefore requires disclosure of the record in the general route, but it does not set a reconciliation period or make the transportation exception available to remote applications generally.

- 15 U.S.C. §1681b(b)(3) — Fair Credit Reporting Act, conditions on use of consumer reports for employment purposes.
- https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/15/1681b

### evidence.probation_period_limits_and_dismissal_standards_ukraine_labour_code_art_26_28 — Probation period limits and dismissal standards (Ukraine, Labour Code art. 26–28)

Articles 26–28 of the Labour Code of Ukraine (Кодекс законів про працю України) establish statutory boundaries for probationary periods: probation may not exceed three months for standard employees (or six months in exceptional cases agreed with trade unions). If the probation period expires and the employee continues working, they are deemed to have passed probation, and subsequent dismissal is permitted only under standard general grounds. During probation, an employer finding that the employee does not meet the role or work may dismiss on that ground after giving written notice three days in advance; the employee may challenge the termination through the labour-dispute procedure.

- Кодекс законів про працю України, статті 26, 27, 28 (Випробування при прийнятті на роботу, строк випробування, наслідки результату випробування).
- https://zakon.rada.gov.ua/laws/show/322-08

### evidence.promissory_estoppel_and_pre_employment_good_faith_restatement_of_employment_law_2_02 — Promissory Estoppel and Pre-Employment Good Faith (Restatement of Employment Law § 2.02)

Section 2.02 of the Restatement of Employment Law (American Law Institute, 2015) and prevailing common-law promissory estoppel doctrines establish actionable employer liability when an employer makes representations of an existing, funded position to induce a prospective employee to incur detrimental reliance (e.g. resigning from prior employment, incurring moving costs) while knowing the underlying headcount authorization or budgetary certification had not been secured or had lapsed.

- Restatement of Employment Law § 2.02 (Promise of Employment: Reliance and Revocation) (American Law Institute, 2015).
- https://www.ali.org/publications/restatement-law/employment-law

### evidence.publishing_the_band_before_the_interview_becomes_a_duty_in_the_eu_directive_2023_970_art_5 — Publishing the band before the interview becomes a duty in the EU (Directive 2023/970, Art. 5)

EU law requires employers to give applicants the initial pay or its range for the advertised position, set on objective and gender-neutral criteria, "in a manner such as to ensure an informed and transparent negotiation on pay, such as in a published job vacancy notice, prior to the job interview or otherwise", and to state the applicable collective agreement where there is one. It also forbids asking an applicant about their pay history in current or previous employment, and requires vacancy notices and job titles to be gender-neutral. The directive is being transposed into national law across Member States, and the reporting duties in Article 9 begin on 7 June 2027 for the largest employers. It fixes when a number must be disclosed, not that the number cannot move afterwards.

- Directive (EU) 2023/970 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May 2023, Article 5 (Pay transparency prior to employment).
- https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/970/oj/eng

### evidence.quits_rate_information_sector_bls_jolts — Quits rate, information sector (BLS JOLTS)

The seasonally adjusted quits rate in the US information sector was 1.1% in June 2026 (preliminary), down from 1.9% in June 2022: fewer seats are being vacated by the people already in them.

- US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, series JTS510000000000000QUR (Quits rate, information, seasonally adjusted).
- https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/JTS510000000000000QUR

### evidence.rev_proc_2025_28_irs — Rev. Proc. 2025-28 (IRS)

IRS guidance on the 2025 restoration: foreign research or experimental expenditures keep the 15-year amortisation period; balances capitalised under the 2022–2024 rules may be recovered in full in the first tax year beginning after 31 December 2024 or ratably over two years; and a taxpayer meeting the section 448(c) gross-receipts test — $31,000,000 average annual gross receipts over the three prior tax years for a year beginning in 2025 — may elect the new treatment retroactively to tax years beginning after 31 December 2021, by 6 July 2026.

- Internal Revenue Service, Rev. Proc. 2025-28, Internal Revenue Bulletin 2025-38, sections 2.02, 2.03(1), 2.06 and 3.02(1).
- https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-28.pdf

### evidence.salary_transparency_growth_slows_but_momentum_continues_indeed_hiring_lab — Salary Transparency: Growth Slows, but Momentum Continues (Indeed Hiring Lab)

Tracks the share of US job postings on Indeed that disclose pay: 57.8% in September 2024, up from 52.2% a year earlier, with wide variation by occupation. Roughly four in ten postings still omit compensation — the structural precondition for compensation-band discrepancies surfacing only at late stages.

- Indeed Hiring Lab (2024, October 23). Salary Transparency: Growth Slows, but Momentum Continues.
- https://hiringlab.indeed.com/2024/10/23/salary-transparency-growth-slows-but-momentum-continues/

### evidence.self_selected_survey_of_it_job_seekers_in_one_national_market_dou — Self-selected survey of IT job seekers in one national market (DOU)

A web survey run on a national IT community site in March–April 2026, covering 3,777 professionals in the country, 943 working abroad, and 363 looking for a first job in the field. Respondents were not sampled: they answered a questionnaire published on a site they already read, and the publication states no recruitment method, response rate or weighting. It describes who chose to answer, which is a different population from everyone searching.

- Більше пошуку, менше оптимізму: як змінився ІТ-ринок праці — результати опитування DOU, 2026.
- https://dou.ua/lenta/articles/job-market-2026-part-1/

### evidence.seniority_mix_of_software_postings_indeed_hiring_lab — Seniority mix of software postings (Indeed Hiring Lab)

Senior-level roles accounted for 69.3% of software development postings and entry-level roles for 4.5% in the first quarter of 2026, measured on one job board's postings rather than on all vacancies.

- Indeed Hiring Lab, The Labor Market Is Tilting Toward Seniority, 23 July 2026.
- https://hiringlab.indeed.com/2026/07/23/the-labor-market-is-tilting-toward-seniority/

### evidence.stated_requirements_set_above_what_current_jobholders_hold_hbs_dismissed_by_degrees — Stated requirements set above what current jobholders hold (HBS, Dismissed by Degrees)

Across 26 million job postings, 67% of postings for production supervisor asked for a college degree while 16% of the people then doing that job held one — a gap of 51 percentage points between what the posting required and what the role demonstrably ran on. The study covers middle-skill occupations in the United States, not software roles, so it evidences the mechanism — a requirement list assembled from something other than the work being done — rather than any figure for technical hiring. The report also surveyed 600 business and HR leaders.

- Fuller, J. B., & Raman, M. (2017). Dismissed by Degrees: How degree inflation is undermining U.S. competitiveness and hurting America's middle class. Harvard Business School, Accenture and Grads of Life, October 2017.
- https://www.hbs.edu/news/releases/degree-inflation-us-competetiveness

### evidence.statutory_notice_and_contractual_probation_parameters_uk_employment_rights_act_1996 — Statutory minimum notice (UK, Employment Rights Act 1996 §86)

Section 86 of the UK Employment Rights Act 1996 sets statutory minimum notice periods once an employee has been continuously employed for at least one month, with longer employer notice minima based on completed service. The section does not define probation, govern withdrawal before employment starts, or establish why an employer uses a probation clause.

- UK Employment Rights Act 1996, Section 86 (Rights of employer and employee to minimum notice).
- https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1996/18/section/86

### evidence.structured_selection_procedures_and_evaluator_preparation_29_c_f_r_1607_4_eu_ai_act_annex_iii — Selection-procedure impact records and oversight of high-risk recruitment AI

The EEOC Uniform Guidelines require users of employee-selection procedures to maintain information about adverse impact and, where adverse impact exists, address validity and alternatives. The EU AI Act classifies specified AI used in recruitment or selection as high-risk and requires effective human oversight of such systems. Neither source mandates preparation time, a tie-break rule, or a rota for an ordinary human interview panel; those remain design proposals requiring separate effectiveness evidence.

- EEOC Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures, 29 C.F.R. Part 1607 §§4, 15; Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Annex III(4)(a) and Article 14.
- https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/subtitle-B/chapter-XIV/part-1607

### evidence.technology_ipo_profitability_1980_2025_ritter — Technology IPO profitability, 1980–2025 (Ritter)

Of 121 US technology listings in 2021, 21% were profitable on trailing- twelve-month earnings. The profitable share ranged from 15% to 43% in every year from 2011 to 2021, so a listing route remained open to companies without trailing profits throughout the period.

- Ritter, Jay R. (2026). Initial Public Offerings: Technology Stock IPOs, Table 4b — Technology and Life Science Company IPOs, 1980–2025. University of Florida.
- https://web.archive.org/web/20260731141233/https://site.warrington.ufl.edu/ritter/files/IPOs-Tech.pdf

### evidence.the_algorithmic_barrier_quantifying_frictional_unemployment_in_automated_recruitment_fofanah_2026 — The Algorithmic Barrier: Quantifying Frictional Unemployment in Automated Recruitment (Fofanah, 2026)

Benchmarks a legacy keyword-based ATS parser against a proposed semantic matching system on the same applicant pool. The legacy system's recall is 0.45 (vs. 0.92 for the semantic system) — meaning most qualified candidates in the pool are never surfaced to a reviewer. The paper's error-mode analysis attributes over 40% of the legacy system's false negatives to pure lexical variation: a candidate's CV describing work in different wording from the posting's exact required terms (e.g. "client engagement" where the rubric expects "customer success"), not a genuine skills gap.

- Fofanah, I. D. (2026). The Algorithmic Barrier: Quantifying Artificial Frictional Unemployment and Information Asymmetry in Automated Recruitment Systems. arXiv:2601.14534.
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14534

### evidence.too_good_to_hire_capability_and_inferences_about_commitment_in_labor_markets — Too Good to Hire? Capability and Inferences about Commitment in Labor Markets

Four experiments with hiring managers show that candidates signalling more capability than the role requires are perceived as less committed to the organization and are penalized in hiring decisions — direct evidence for "overqualified" rejections and the seniority double bind.

- Galperin, R. V., Hahl, O., Sterling, A. D., & Guo, J. (2020). Administrative Science Quarterly, 65(2), 275–313.
- https://doi.org/10.1177/0001839219840022

### evidence.tracked_technology_layoffs_layoffs_fyi — Tracked technology layoffs (Layoffs.fyi)

A privately maintained tracker that compiles publicly reported layoff events at technology and startup companies worldwide, revised as new reports arrive. It is not a statistical census. It records 165,269 employees in 2022, 265,660 in 2023, 152,922 in 2024, 122,606 in 2025 and 127,180 between 1 January and 24 August 2026.

- Layoffs.fyi — Tech and Startup Layoff Tracker, per-year pages, retrieved 27 August 2026.
- https://layoffs.fyi/2026-layoffs/

### evidence.us_information_sector_employment_bls_ces — US information-sector employment (BLS CES)

US payroll employment in the information sector (NAICS 51 — software publishing, data processing and telecommunications, but not computer systems design) fell from a November 2022 peak of 3,115,000 to 2,780,000 in July 2026, a decline of 335,000 or 10.8%. An official establishment survey, not a layoff tracker.

- US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Employment Statistics, series CES5000000001 (All employees, thousands, information, seasonally adjusted).
- https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/CES5000000001

### evidence.whether_an_application_was_assessed_at_all_is_defined_in_regulation_41_cfr_60_1_3 — Whether an application was assessed at all is defined in regulation (41 CFR 60-1.3)

US federal contracting regulation turns on whether an expression of interest was actually assessed. An individual counts as an "Internet Applicant" only where, among four criteria, "the contractor considers the individual for employment in a particular position" — defined as assessing the substantive information provided against the qualifications for that position. The rule then states the converse plainly: where there is a large number of expressions of interest, the contractor does *not* consider an individual by using "data management techniques that do not depend on assessment of qualifications, such as random sampling or absolute numerical limits, to reduce the number of expressions of interest to be considered". So an application closed without being read is a category the law already names and treats differently from a reviewed decline. The rule binds federal contractors in the United States, it governs who must be counted rather than what a candidate is told, and it does not require a contractor to record why any individual went unconsidered.

- 41 C.F.R. §60-1.3, definition of "Internet Applicant", paragraphs (1)-(3). Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs.
- https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-41/subtitle-B/chapter-60/part-60-1/subpart-A/section-60-1.3

## Validated scenario compositions

### scenario.application_silence — Application followed by silence

- Observations: obs.complete_silence_after_submission, obs.rejection_after_the_application_sat_pending_for_months
- Compatible barriers: bar.application_ingestion, bar.automated_filter_parser_threshold, bar.inbound_screening_triage
- Compatible mechanisms: mech.stale_or_orphaned_job_requisition, mech.automated_application_expiration_timeout, mech.ats_parser_extraction_failure, mech.recruiter_volume_quota_incentive_distortion, mech.speculative_sourcing_talent_pooling_without_opening
- Does NOT establish: The recruiter deliberately ghosted the candidate.
- Does NOT establish: The application was read and rejected on its merits.
- Does NOT establish: The requisition was open at the moment the application arrived.

### scenario.ats_knockout — Automated Parsing Knockout

Instant rejection outside business hours combined with rigid uncontextualized filters.

- Observations: obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template, obs.explicit_feedback_citing_skill_depth_shortfall, obs.unsolicited_recruiter_outreach_followed_by_ghosting

### scenario.client_site_vendor_constraint — Vendor process blocked by client-site terms

A vendor process advances through internal screening, then the client gate reveals that the work must be performed at a client site or under a client-controlled schedule.

- Observations: obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template, obs.rejection_naming_a_specific_industry_sector_as_required
- Compatible barriers: bar.client_profile_approval_and_client_interview, bar.recruiter_screening_call, bar.technical_screen_live_assessment
- Compatible mechanisms: mech.domain_specificity_over_weighting, mech.location_or_timezone_compliance_constraint, mech.bid_conditional_talent_pool
- Does NOT establish: The vendor can unilaterally waive the client's site or schedule condition.
- Does NOT establish: A generic vendor rejection proves that the candidate failed the vendor's technical screen.
- Does NOT establish: The client-site requirement is ownerless just because it is invisible to the candidate at first.

### scenario.closed_then_reposted — Rejected, then the same role is posted again

- Observations: obs.position_closed_after_final_interview_without_hire, obs.materially_similar_role_reposted_shortly_after_rejection, obs.republished_job_posting_with_refreshed_date_and_identical_requirement_body
- Compatible barriers: bar.headcount_executive_budget_approval, bar.requisition_approval_public_posting
- Compatible mechanisms: mech.headcount_freeze_or_budget_cancellation, mech.mid_process_role_requirement_redefinition, mech.pre_selected_internal_candidate, mech.stale_or_orphaned_job_requisition
- Does NOT establish: The reposted requisition is the same requisition.
- Does NOT establish: The candidate was rejected in order to hire someone already chosen.
- Does NOT establish: The employer acted in bad faith.

### scenario.downlevelling_trap — Down-Levelling & Delayed Start

Scope expansion, sub-band compensation offer, and post-acceptance start date slippage.

- Observations: obs.rejection_naming_a_jurisdiction_or_work_eligibility_ground, obs.rejection_naming_a_specific_industry_sector_as_required, obs.offer_accepted_followed_by_delayed_start_date_or_post_signing_revocation

### scenario.ghost_refresh — Ghost Requisition & Pipeline Refresh

Stale posting refreshed with identical body while active applicants experience silence.

- Observations: obs.complete_silence_after_submission, obs.materially_similar_role_reposted_shortly_after_rejection, obs.republished_job_posting_with_refreshed_date_and_identical_requirement_body

### scenario.hybrid_cadence_disclosed_late — Hybrid cadence appears after screening

A candidate passes the first compatibility checks, then the process closes because a fixed office cadence or city anchor was not stated early enough to be evaluated before the screen.

- Observations: obs.rejection_naming_a_jurisdiction_or_work_eligibility_ground, obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template
- Compatible barriers: bar.recruiter_screening_call, bar.inbound_screening_triage
- Compatible mechanisms: mech.location_or_timezone_compliance_constraint, mech.hidden_evaluation_rubric_or_undisclosed_priority
- Does NOT establish: The word hybrid is enough to disclose the weekly attendance burden.
- Does NOT establish: The candidate rejected the employer rather than failing an undisclosed condition.
- Does NOT establish: The attendance rule proves a lack of skill or interest.

### scenario.post_panel_freeze — Post-Panel Freeze & Silence

Strong verbal engagement followed by multi-week offer hold and sudden ghosting.

- Observations: obs.complete_silence_after_submission, obs.multiple_interview_reschedulings_or_interviewer_no_show, obs.rejection_naming_an_internal_hire_as_the_outcome

### scenario.remote_country_payroll_mismatch — Remote role, country payroll mismatch

A role is presented as remote, the screen proceeds normally, and the closing reason later names residence, work eligibility, or an unsupported contracting country.

- Observations: obs.rejection_naming_a_jurisdiction_or_work_eligibility_ground
- Compatible barriers: bar.recruiter_screening_call, bar.offer_closing_contract_execution
- Compatible mechanisms: mech.location_or_timezone_compliance_constraint, mech.hidden_evaluation_rubric_or_undisclosed_priority
- Does NOT establish: The remote label means the employer can issue a contract in every country.
- Does NOT establish: The jurisdiction ground proves that no technical or cohort evaluation happened.
- Does NOT establish: The recruiter personally controls the payroll coverage list.

### scenario.remote_timezone_overlap_limit — Remote role bounded by timezone overlap

A role can be performed remotely, but the process closes when the team requires overlap hours that the candidate cannot reliably cover.

- Observations: obs.rejection_naming_a_jurisdiction_or_work_eligibility_ground, obs.communication_mismatch_or_tone_friction_in_panel
- Compatible barriers: bar.recruiter_screening_call, bar.team_cross_functional_panel
- Compatible mechanisms: mech.location_or_timezone_compliance_constraint, mech.communication_or_working_style_friction
- Does NOT establish: Remote work implies timezone-neutral work.
- Does NOT establish: Timezone mismatch proves a communication-style defect.
- Does NOT establish: The candidate can solve the overlap requirement without a trade-off.

### scenario.ua_reservation_worksite_constraint — Ukrainian reservation status meets worksite constraint

A Ukrainian hiring process becomes constrained by the interaction between military registration status, employer reservation capacity, and where the role must be performed.

- Observations: obs.rejection_naming_a_jurisdiction_or_work_eligibility_ground, obs.offer_accepted_followed_by_delayed_start_date_or_post_signing_revocation
- Compatible barriers: bar.recruiter_screening_call, bar.offer_closing_contract_execution, bar.reference_background_verification
- Compatible mechanisms: mech.location_or_timezone_compliance_constraint, mech.start_date_slippage_and_post_acceptance_revocation
- Does NOT establish: The military-status constraint proves discriminatory intent.
- Does NOT establish: Every Ukrainian employer can create or waive reservation status for any candidate.
- Does NOT establish: The candidate's registration state is interchangeable with ordinary relocation preference.

## Presentation-only archetype overlays

- **actor.ats_vendor — The Silent Landlord of the Funnel** (systematic/hidden): Sets no policy and hires no one — just ships the defaults that decide what a great many other decisions ever see.
- **actor.candidate — The One With the Least Information and the Most at Stake** (mixed/visible): Sees every stage of their own process and almost none of anyone else's — the only actor for whom this whole atlas exists at all.
- **actor.client — The Boss You'll Never Know You Had** (systematic/hidden): Signs the contract the whole requisition depends on, and holds a gate the candidate is never even told has a name.
- **actor.employer_policy — The Rulemaker Who Never Shows Up** (systematic/hidden): Fixes the bands, authorises the headcount, writes the rules everyone downstream executes — and meets exactly zero candidates while doing it.
- **actor.hiring_manager — Grading You Between Meetings** (ad hoc/visible): Owns the outcome and sets the bar, while doing this alongside the actual job the role exists to do — the panel's calibration is whatever their week left them with.
- **actor.public_policy_and_industry_standards — The Slowest Actor in the Room** (systematic/ambiguous): Public, codified, and knowable in principle — and moving on a timescale no single hiring process will ever wait around to feel.
- **actor.recruiter — Knows Everything, Decides Nothing** (mixed/visible): Holds more information about your process than anyone else in it, and less authority over how it ends than almost anyone else too.
- **bar.application_ingestion — The Database Says Yes** (systematic/hidden): An automated schema check and link to a requisition, often completed before a person reviews the application.
- **bar.automated_filter_parser_threshold — The Score You'll Never See** (systematic/hidden): A number crosses a threshold somewhere in the pipeline, and you find out only which side of it you landed on.
- **bar.client_profile_approval_and_client_interview — A Client You'll Never Meet Grades You Anyway** (systematic/hidden): The sign-off that actually decides belongs to someone the candidate is never introduced to.
- **bar.compensation_levelling_reconciliation — The Spreadsheet That Decides the Level** (systematic/hidden): Your stated expectation gets checked against a band you were never shown, by a process that happens entirely off to the side.
- **bar.headcount_executive_budget_approval — A Committee You've Never Heard Of** (systematic/hidden): Finance and leadership certify the money three approvals before the offer is ever written, in a room the candidate has no reason to know exists.
- **bar.hiring_manager_in_depth_review — One Person's Read on Your Whole Career** (ad hoc/hidden): Seniority, ownership, trade-off reasoning — real dimensions, evaluated by exactly one person's judgment, with no second opinion built into the gate.
- **bar.inbound_screening_triage — Whoever's Queue You Landed In** (ad hoc/hidden): No stated rubric — a person decides whether you're worth a first conversation, and which person that is changes what happens to you.
- **bar.offer_closing_contract_execution — The One Gate You Sign Yourself** (systematic/visible): The rare barrier where the candidate is a required party to the pass condition, not a subject of it.
- **bar.outbound_sourcing_talent_pool_contact — The Message That Started It** (ad hoc/visible): The one gate that begins with the company reaching out, not the candidate applying — you feel it happen because it happens to you directly.
- **bar.probation_period_post_start_confirmation — Still Being Interviewed, Just Employed Now** (systematic/hidden): A statutory evaluation window with a real legal shape, running on judgments the newly-hired employee mostly can't see being made.
- **bar.recruiter_screening_call — The Vibe Check With a Job Title** (ad hoc/visible): Fluency, timeline, tone — assessed live, conversationally, with no rubric standing between the call and the verdict.
- **bar.reference_background_verification — Checked Without You in the Room** (systematic/hidden): Every check clears or it doesn't, in a process the candidate is the subject of and no part of.
- **bar.requisition_approval_public_posting — The Gate That Closes Before You Arrive** (systematic/hidden): The funnel's first barrier, and the only one no candidate is ever present for — by the time you apply, it's already been decided that you could.
- **bar.take_home_work_sample_evaluation — Graded Off-Camera** (systematic/hidden): A stated rubric — architecture, tests, docs — applied by a reviewer you never watch read it.
- **bar.team_cross_functional_panel — A Room Full of People Scoring You Silently** (systematic/hidden): A consensus threshold exists, but what any one panelist actually wrote stays theirs.
- **bar.technical_screen_live_assessment — The One You Can Actually Watch Yourself Pass or Fail** (systematic/visible): Live, synchronous, against a stated threshold — the closest thing in the whole funnel to a test you get to see yourself take.
- **era.a_fixed_number_of_seats — The Recession That Never Shows Up in the Layoff Numbers** (systematic/ambiguous): Layoffs stayed roughly flat while hires fell 29% — the contraction runs through who never gets hired at all, which is exactly the kind of shortage that never makes a headline.
- **era.rates_up_payroll_repriced — The Year Every Posting Wanted Someone Already Doing the Job** (systematic/visible): A rate peak and a tax rule change landed in the same eighteen months, and hiring narrowed to replacing a specific person who had just left — which is why the evidence bar suddenly meant this exact stack, this exact scale, right now.
- **era.the_record_funding_years — When the Funnel Ran Backwards** (systematic/visible): Two years when employers competed for candidates instead of the reverse — shorter loops, bigger offers, a job without a current job as no obstacle at all.
- **era.zero_rates_and_a_same_year_deduction — The Decade When Junior Was Cheap to Bet On** (systematic/ambiguous): Seven years at the policy floor and a same-year tax deduction made an empty seat more expensive than a wrong hire — a decade of demand policy nobody applying for a job ever had to read to benefit from.
- **int.a_named_decider_and_a_written_rule_for_a_split_panel — Someone Has to Break the Tie** (systematic/visible): A named decider before the panel splits, so the outcome is a rule applied instead of a vote nobody remembers taking.
- **int.auto_close_stale_job_requisitions — The Listing Cleans Up After Itself** (systematic/hidden): A posting that expires itself the moment headcount lapses, instead of outliving the search by months.
- **int.bench_availability_declared_at_each_stage_gate — The Bench Has to Announce Itself** (systematic/visible): The internal option is stated at every gate it passes, with a date — so a bench fill can never look like a search that simply vanished.
- **int.candidate_ats_parser_conformance_test_utility — Test Your Résumé Against the Machine First** (systematic/visible): The same parser that will read your CV, handed to you before you submit it.
- **int.candidate_work_index_submitted_with_the_application — A Table of Contents for Your Own Work** (systematic/visible): One page naming exactly where the real work is, opened in the first minutes — so the screener never has to guess which repository is yours.
- **int.contractable_jurisdictions_listed_in_the_posting — The Map Comes With the Job Ad** (systematic/visible): The jurisdictions the company can actually hire in, named before the first call — not discovered after three rounds.
- **int.critique_injected_on_script_in_the_collaborative_exercise — Everyone Gets the Same Curveball** (systematic/hidden): The same objection, at the same point, scripted for every candidate — fair precisely because you'll never know it was rehearsed.
- **int.dated_funding_certification_before_the_final_round — No Final Round Without the Money Being Real** (systematic/hidden): A funding date checked live before the last interview is booked, so the panel that likes you can't be overruled by a budget nobody re-confirmed.
- **int.disqualifying_criteria_published_with_the_posting — The Filter's Rules, Printed on the Box** (systematic/visible): Every acronym and year-count the automated gate checks for, listed in the posting — a deterministic filter stops being a secret the moment it's published.
- **int.distinct_closure_status_for_unreviewed_applications — Told the Truth: Nobody Opened It** (systematic/visible): A status that says exactly what happened — closed unread — instead of borrowing the label used for an application someone actually considered.
- **int.domain_requirement_carries_a_stated_ramp_time — How Long It Actually Takes to Learn** (systematic/visible): A stated ramp time turns a hard requirement into what it actually is — a preference, scored honestly instead of gating on a technicality.
- **int.internal_candidacy_stated_in_the_posting — Naming the Internal Candidate Out Loud** (systematic/visible): If the seat already has a name attached, the posting says so — and says what the external search is actually deciding.
- **int.interview_seats_booked_with_prep_time_and_a_second_name_on_the_rota — A Backup Interviewer, Just in Case** (systematic/hidden): A second name on the rota, so one overloaded engineer's sprint doesn't become your third rescheduled round.
- **int.outreach_states_the_requisition_behind_it — Naming the Req in the First Message** (systematic/visible): The recruiter's opening line states what they're actually recruiting against — an approved role, or a pool built on a forecast.
- **int.publish_the_technical_screen_s_columns_and_threshold_before_the_round — The Rubric, Published Before You Walk In** (systematic/visible): The columns, the weights, the passing threshold — printed next to the posting instead of existing only in the panel's heads.
- **int.recorded_finalist_standing_with_a_dated_re_entry_route — A Second Chance, With a Date on It** (systematic/visible): Clearing the bar and not getting the offer becomes a recorded standing with a real re-entry date, not a story that ends at rejection.
- **int.remove_career_gap_feature_from_automated_ranking_models — Deleted From the Algorithm, Quietly** (systematic/hidden): The gap penalty doesn't get explained or disclosed — it gets removed from the model, which is the more honest fix.
- **int.requirement_changes_versioned_and_sent_to_candidates_in_flight — You Get a Changelog Too** (systematic/visible): When the role changes mid-search, everyone already in the pipeline gets told what changed and which of their completed rounds still counts.
- **int.requirements_drawn_from_the_team_s_own_backlog — Every Requirement Traces to a Real Ticket** (systematic/visible): Drawn from two quarters of the team's actual backlog — and anything that doesn't trace to a task gets published separately, unscreened.
- **int.screening_note_bound_to_observations_and_disposition_codes — The Note Can Only Say What It Saw** (systematic/hidden): A screening note restricted to what the record actually shows, closed with a fixed code — no room left for an impression to pass as a finding.
- **int.standardized_late_stage_rejection_feedback_taxonomy — A Real Reason, From a Real Menu** (systematic/visible): Structured categories replace the generic template — a stated reason instead of a form letter shaped like one.
- **int.strict_take_home_timebox_blinded_evaluation_rubric — Three Hours, Graded Blind** (systematic/visible): A hard timebox, paid compensation for anything longer, and a reviewer who doesn't know whose submission they're reading.
- **int.upfront_compensation_band_disclosure — The Band, Published Before You Ask** (systematic/visible): The number that ends the compensation double bind before it starts — stated in the posting, not extracted from the candidate first.
- **int.verification_discrepancy_disclosure_and_reconciliation_window — Both Numbers, Shown Side by Side** (systematic/visible): The discrepancy the check found, and what the candidate's own record says, released together — with time to reconcile them before the offer dies.
- **loop.employment_gap_penalty_loop — The Gap That Feeds Itself** (systematic/hidden): A downranking and a keyword filter amplifying each other in a closed loop — every rejection the gap causes makes the gap look worse to the next algorithm that reads it.
- **loop.inflated_requirements_search_saturation_loop — The Search That Outlasts Its Own Reason** (ad hoc/visible): Requirements too high filter out the people who'd fit, the search drags, the team gets tired of it and redefines the role — which resets the filter that started the whole loop.
- **loop.take_home_opportunity_cost_saturation_loop — Everyone's Too Busy for Everyone Else** (ad hoc/hidden): Overloaded interviewers move rounds and read submissions fast; unbounded take-homes eat the hours that would have gone to more applications — each side of the loop makes the other side worse.
- **mech.ats_parser_extraction_failure — Lost in Translation** (mixed/hidden): A parser doing exactly what it was built to do to a résumé it was never tested against — nobody chose this outcome, and nobody sees it happen.
- **mech.automated_application_expiration_timeout — The 60-Day Countdown** (systematic/hidden): A clock the candidate never sees start, counting down to a rejection that will look exactly like every other one.
- **mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter — Missing the Magic Word** (systematic/ambiguous): A binary filter keyed to one exact acronym or year count — provable if you know to check the posting against the filter, invisible if you don't.
- **mech.bench_priority_fill — The Bench Beat You To It** (systematic/hidden): A standard internal-mobility policy, working exactly as designed — the search was real, and so was the seat that had already been informally filled.
- **mech.bid_conditional_talent_pool — Hired for a Job That Doesn't Exist Yet** (systematic/hidden): The search is real and the role is not — recruiters build pipeline against a contract that may never be signed, and nothing in the posting says so.
- **mech.communication_or_working_style_friction — The Personality Test You Didn't Know You Took** (ad hoc/visible): No rubric, no calibration between panels — just one interviewer's read on tone, formed live and rarely written down the same way twice.
- **mech.domain_specificity_over_weighting — Wrong Flavor of Experience** (ad hoc/ambiguous): One interviewer's exact-vertical preference standing in for transferable depth — you might feel the pushback in the room, but never see it scored.
- **mech.employment_gap_downranking_bias — The Gap Tax** (systematic/hidden): Verified project history counts for less than a blank stretch on the calendar, applied by a ranking system the candidate never sees run.
- **mech.experience_age_grading_mismatch — Too Senior to Stay** (ad hoc/hidden): A forecast about your future boredom, written into a screening note you will never read, standing in for an assessment of the work in front of them.
- **mech.genuine_technical_skill_shortfall — The Honest One** (systematic/visible): The mandatory honest-baseline entry: sometimes the bar really is the bar, and the candidate's own performance in the room is the whole story.
- **mech.headcount_freeze_or_budget_cancellation — The Budget Got There First** (systematic/ambiguous): A finance decision made three floors up from the panel that liked you — sometimes named honestly, sometimes indistinguishable from being ghosted.
- **mech.hidden_evaluation_rubric_or_undisclosed_priority — The Rubric Nobody Published** (systematic/hidden): A real rubric, scored consistently — just never written into the posting or said out loud in the round.
- **mech.hiring_manager_consensus_impasse — Lost the Tie You Never Knew Existed** (systematic/hidden): A real governance rule — no consensus defaults to no hire — deciding an outcome the candidate will only ever read as an ordinary rejection.
- **mech.inflated_requisition_requirements_vs_actual_team_needs — Ten Technologies for a Two-Technology Job** (systematic/visible): The proof is the posting itself — a Staff-level bar stacked onto work that is, by its own description, feature delivery.
- **mech.interview_resource_scheduling_saturation — Sat In On Someone Else's Sprint** (ad hoc/visible): The interviewer had a sprint commitment before they had you — the reschedule, the cold read, the dropped round are all things you actually felt happen.
- **mech.location_or_timezone_compliance_constraint — Right Candidate, Wrong Country** (systematic/visible): Not a judgment about the candidate at all — a legal-entity gap that a company can, and often does, simply name out loud.
- **mech.mid_process_role_requirement_redefinition — The Role You Interviewed For Doesn't Exist Anymore** (ad hoc/hidden): The stack, the level or the scope moved while you were mid-pipeline, and the assessment you already passed was for a role that no longer exists.
- **mech.portfolio_work_artifact_misinterpretation — Looked in the Wrong Repo** (ad hoc/hidden): The real work exists, in a layout or an organisation the screener never opened — a filing accident standing in for a verdict on the work itself.
- **mech.pre_selected_internal_candidate — The Posting Was a Formality** (systematic/hidden): Advertised to satisfy a policy, not to find someone — the seat was filled before the listing ever went up, and nothing in it says so.
- **mech.probation_used_as_extended_de_facto_interview — The Interview That Kept Going After You Signed** (systematic/ambiguous): The bar quietly drops before the offer and quietly returns after it — you find out which interview you were actually in only if it ends.
- **mech.recruiter_volume_quota_incentive_distortion — Read at the Speed of the Queue** (systematic/hidden): Five hundred applications and one shift to clear them — a real triage process, running exactly as the incentive built it to, that the candidate never gets to watch happen.
- **mech.reference_check_discrepancy_or_regulatory_ineligibility — The Check That Didn't Come Back Clean** (systematic/ambiguous): A formal verification step with a real outcome — you know your own history, but rarely which line of it the checker couldn't confirm.
- **mech.speculative_sourcing_talent_pooling_without_opening — Recruited for a Headcount That Doesn't Exist** (systematic/hidden): A conversation opened, a pool built, against a headcount that finance never actually approved — indistinguishable, from the outside, from a real search.
- **mech.stale_or_orphaned_job_requisition — Nobody Remembered to Close It** (mixed/hidden): Not a decision — an omission. The listing outlives the search that opened it because closing it was nobody's specific job.
- **mech.start_date_slippage_and_post_acceptance_revocation — Hired, Then Un-Hired** (ad hoc/visible): The one part of this you actually see happen — a signed date moving, or an offer pulled, between the handshake and day one.
- **mech.stronger_competing_candidate_in_final_cohort — Someone Else Needed Less Ramp-Up** (systematic/hidden): You cleared every bar — someone else cleared them with less onboarding cost attached, and you'll never be told who.
- **mech.take_home_evaluation_fatigue_asymmetry — Fifteen Hours, Ninety Seconds** (ad hoc/hidden): The asymmetry is the whole mechanism — the time you spent and the time it got reviewed were never going to be the same number, and you'll never know the second one.
- **mech.unstated_compensation_band_discrepancy — The Band That Was Never Written Down** (systematic/hidden): A real budget ceiling, set before the search opened and never shared with the candidate — the gap it creates looks like rejection, not arithmetic.
- **obs.communication_mismatch_or_tone_friction_in_panel — Vibes, Officially Noted** (ad hoc/hidden): A feeling in the room, recorded as if it were data — the observation is real, but it explains nothing about why.
- **obs.compensation_band_reduced_or_altered_mid_process — The Number Moved** (systematic/visible): One of the few observations that is also, on its own, most of the evidence — a stated figure that became a different stated figure.
- **obs.complete_silence_after_submission — The Loudest Nothing** (mixed/hidden): A common and exceptionally low-information observation — an absence compatible with almost everything.
- **obs.conflicting_feedback_across_different_interviewers — Two Verdicts, One Candidate** (systematic/visible): Put the two rounds' notes side by side and the contradiction argues itself — the rare observation where the evidence is self-sufficient.
- **obs.explicit_feedback_citing_skill_depth_shortfall — The Itemized Rejection** (systematic/visible): A structured note naming a specific deficit — the honest-baseline observation, stated plainly enough to be checked against your own performance.
- **obs.feedback_naming_as_absent_something_the_submitted_work_contains — They Didn't Open the File** (systematic/ambiguous): A specific, falsifiable claim — checkable against your own submission, but only if you think to go back and check.
- **obs.feedback_stating_candidate_is_overqualified_for_the_grade — Too Much, On the Record** (systematic/visible): The reason is stated in plain language — which is what makes it possible to notice, months later, that the opposite reason arrived from somewhere else.
- **obs.generic_closer_alignment_rejection_template — The Template Everyone Gets** (systematic/hidden): A familiar document that establishes almost nothing: a form letter shaped like an explanation.
- **obs.materially_similar_role_reposted_shortly_after_rejection — Still Advertised** (mixed/visible): An observation you can verify independently on a public job board — what it means once verified is a separate question.
- **obs.multiple_interview_reschedulings_or_interviewer_no_show — Rescheduled Into Oblivion** (ad hoc/visible): You watched it happen, calendar invite by calendar invite — what you can't see is whether it was one overloaded interviewer or the whole process falling apart.
- **obs.offer_accepted_followed_by_delayed_start_date_or_post_signing_revocation — Signed, Then Stalled** (ad hoc/visible): A date moving, or a signature quietly not mattering — the one part of the whole funnel you watch happen to you in real time, after you thought it was over.
- **obs.offer_rescinded_or_delayed_due_to_internal_freeze — The Offer That Un-Happened** (systematic/ambiguous): Sometimes named for what it is — a freeze — and sometimes left to read exactly like every other kind of silence.
- **obs.position_closed_after_final_interview_without_hire — Everyone Passed and Then So Did the Job** (mixed/ambiguous): You cleared the whole funnel and the funnel itself disappeared — cancelled, frozen or closed are three different stories that read identically from where you're standing.
- **obs.rejection_after_the_application_sat_pending_for_months — Filed and Forgotten** (systematic/ambiguous): A measurable fact — six weeks, no contact, no stage entered — that narrows the field of causes without naming one of them.
- **obs.rejection_naming_a_jurisdiction_or_work_eligibility_ground — It Was Never About the Work** (systematic/visible): The reason is named in the message itself — where you live, not what you can do — which is exactly what makes it checkable against the posting's own claims.
- **obs.rejection_naming_a_specific_industry_sector_as_required — Right Skills, Wrong Logo** (systematic/visible): The stated reason names a sector, not a skill — visible enough to compare against what the role actually asked a person to do.
- **obs.rejection_naming_an_internal_hire_as_the_outcome — The Seat Was Never Empty** (systematic/visible): One of the few closing messages that names an actual outcome instead of a template — which is what makes it possible to ask what an external posting was for.
- **obs.rejection_within_minutes_of_application_submission — Rejected Before Anyone Could Have Read It** (systematic/visible): The arithmetic does the work here — minutes between submission and rejection is a number you can read straight off two timestamps.
- **obs.republished_job_posting_with_refreshed_date_and_identical_requirement_body — Same Job, New Coat of Paint** (mixed/visible): A timestamp changed and nothing else did — checkable by anyone willing to compare two snapshots of the same listing.
- **obs.take_home_assignment_exceeding_reasonable_stated_scope — The Take-Home That Wasn't** (systematic/visible): A budget was stated in hours and the ask wasn't — the mismatch is arithmetic you can do yourself before you start typing.
- **obs.unsolicited_recruiter_outreach_followed_by_ghosting — Chased, Then Dropped** (ad hoc/visible): You didn't apply — they found you, said so enthusiastically, and then the enthusiasm simply stopped the moment you answered.
- **pat.closed_then_reposted_requisition_motif — The Boomerang Requisition** (mixed/hidden): Could be an abandoned req nobody closed properly, or a rubric nobody disclosed — the generic template gives no way to tell which.
- **pat.compensation_double_bind — Show Your Hand First** (systematic/ambiguous): A completely standard script, asked in plain sight — the unfairness is in what it structurally withholds, not in how it's asked.
- **pat.experience_age_impossibility — The Time Traveler Requirement** (systematic/visible): An automated rule enforcing a threshold no human could have met — the rare hiring claim you can disprove with a release date, not an opinion.
- **pat.seniority_double_bind — The Impossible Middle** (systematic/ambiguous): Two rejections, two reasonable-sounding reasons, no level in between where either applies — the trap is only visible once you set them side by side.
- **proc.an_application_inside_the_ats — The Machine You Never Get to Watch** (systematic/hidden): Four different ways an application can end without a human ever reading it — all of them happening in a system built for exactly this candidate to never see.
- **proc.client_account_hiring_funnel — A Second Funnel, Layered on Top of the First** (systematic/hidden): Runs on its own contract, its own approval, its own silent way of closing — a whole parallel process the candidate experiences as just one more delay.
- **proc.the_hiring_funnel_end_to_end — The Whole Thing, As Far As You Can See It** (systematic/ambiguous): The complete funnel, headcount to signature, with the one variable that actually matters written in at every step: what you, specifically, can see from where you're standing.
- **proc.the_path_as_it_is_supposed_to_run — The Version of This Where Every Promise Gets Kept** (systematic/visible): Not a prediction and not a rule — the baseline every barrier in this registry is measured against, the one path where nothing quietly stops being true.
- **record.annual_engineering_department_budget — The Number Nobody Outside Finance Sees** (systematic/hidden): The top of the whole financial chain that ends in your paycheck, and the one figure in it you will never be shown.
- **record.approved_requisition_funding — Approved, Never Announced** (systematic/hidden): The headcount and band exist, signed off, before the posting ever goes up — and stay exactly as invisible as the posting itself is silent about them.
- **record.candidate_liquid_savings — The Clock Only You Can See** (mixed/visible): A candidate-controlled financial fact that constrains how long a search can continue without new income.
- **record.candidate_search_runway — How Long You Can Afford to Say No** (mixed/visible): Savings divided by burn, in months — the number that quietly decides which offers get a real no and which get accepted out of arithmetic.
- **record.client_project_budget — The Client's Number, Never Shared Down the Chain** (systematic/hidden): A budget line that funds the whole search, held one level further away from the candidate than even the recruiter's own numbers.
- **record.client_services_agreement — The Contract Setting Your Price Before You're Hired** (systematic/hidden): The billing rate and seat scope are fixed in a commercial agreement before you're ever interviewed — the number this negotiates is not the one on your offer letter.
- **record.contingency_placement_fee_commitment — The Recruiter's Bet on You Surviving Ninety Days** (ad hoc/hidden): A fee that isn't earned at the hire — it's earned if you're still there past warranty, which ties the recruiter's incentive to your first few months, not just your first day.
- **record.direct_engineering_payroll — The Number That Reaches Your Account** (systematic/visible): At the end of a chain of largely hidden budgets, this is the figure that reaches the employee's account.
- **record.employer_hiring_and_sourcing_budget — What They Budgeted to Find You** (systematic/hidden): A whole operating line exists just to fund the search that found you — agency fees, sourcing costs — and none of it appears anywhere you'd read it.
- **record.external_agency_settlement — The Fee That Changes Hands Without You** (systematic/hidden): Money settles between the company and the agency on the strength of your hire, in a transaction you are the subject of and no party to.
- **record.search_month_burn_allocation — What Each Month of Looking Actually Costs** (mixed/visible): Rent, tools, the coffee at the interview — a real monthly number the candidate tracks, whether or not anyone else in the funnel ever thinks about it.
- **record.subcontractor_compensation — Your Half of the Invoice** (systematic/visible): The company bills the client one number and pays you a smaller one — this record is your half, the only half you're actually shown.
- **record.vendor_margin_and_headcount_allocation — The Split Between What They Bill and What You're Paid** (systematic/hidden): One internal record holds both numbers at once — the client's billing rate and your compensation — and only ever shows you which side of the split you're on.
